931	          drainBufferedEvents();
932	          notificationVersionAtStart = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
933	          return;
934	        }
935	
936	        // Flush any named events that landed in the ring *during* the
937	        // snapshot build before allocating the marker id. Without this,
938	        // the marker's id would leapfrog those events and the next
939	        // drain (which uses lastDeliveredId = marker.id) would treat
940	        // them as already-delivered, silently dropping them.
941	        drainBufferedEvents();
942	
943	        lastUpdatePayload = serializedPayload;
944	        const version = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
945	        const marker = recordSnapshotMarker(version, runIdScope);
946	        // A named event can still land in the tiny window between the
947	        // pre-marker drain above and marker allocation. Drain only up
948	        // through the id immediately before the marker, then let the
949	        // snapshot frame advance the client to the marker id. Events
950	        // emitted after the marker are delivered by the post-snapshot
951	        // drain below, preserving monotonic SSE ids.
952	        drainBufferedEvents({ throughId: marker.id - 1 });
953	        lastDeliveredId = marker.id;
954	        writeFrame(marker.streamId, "update", serializedPayload);
955	      };
956	
957	      request.signal.addEventListener("abort", () => {
958	        streamClosed = true;
959	      });
960	
961	      // Replay any events the client missed during disconnect. If their
962	      // last id has fallen out of the ring, the resync event tells the
963	      // client to re-bootstrap from /api/events?snapshot=1.
964	      if (resumeFromId !== null) {
965	        drainBufferedEvents();
966	      }
967	
968	      let notificationVersionAtStart = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
969	      // The persisted payload carries no live agent state: every agent in
970	      // it is `bridgeMissing` with empty `pendingElicitations`/
971	      // `pendingPermissions`. That is an acceptable first paint (better
972	      // than a blank screen while the bridge fetch lands), but replaying it
973	      // on every loop iteration makes live-only UI flicker — an open
974	      // elicitation form vanished for the whole runtime-payload build and
975	      // reappeared for the moment the enriched frame was current. Once the
976	      // client has seen live agent state, always wait for the enriched
977	      // payload instead of regressing to the degraded one.
978	      let hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = false;
979	      // Snapshot-rebuild pacing state. `snapshotVersionAtLastBuild` records
980	      // what the build covered, so a wake carrying only delta-only events is
981	      // recognisable and does not force an immediate rebuild.
982	      let snapshotVersionAtLastBuild = getEventStreamSnapshotVersion();
983	      let lastSnapshotBuiltAt = 0;
984	      while (!streamClosed) {
985	        try {
986	          notificationVersionAtStart = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
987	          snapshotVersionAtLastBuild = getEventStreamSnapshotVersion();
988	          lastSnapshotBuiltAt = Date.now();
989	          drainBufferedEvents();
990	          const runtimePayloadPromise = buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions);
991	          const runtimePayload = hasDeliveredRuntimePayload
992	            ? await runtimePayloadPromise
993	            : await Promise.race([
994	              runtimePayloadPromise,
995	              delay(RUNTIME_AGENT_GRACE_MS).then(() => null),
996	            ]);
997	
998	          if (runtimePayload) {
999	            sendUpdateIfChanged(runtimePayload);
1000	            hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = true;
1001	          } else {
1002	            sendUpdateIfChanged(await buildSharedPersistedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions));
1003	            const enrichedPayload = await runtimePayloadPromise;
1004	            if (!streamClosed) {
1005	              sendUpdateIfChanged(enrichedPayload);
1006	              hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = true;
1007	            }
1008	          }
1009	          // Named events emitted during snapshot construction must be
1010	          // flushed before we park; otherwise a worker.* event fired
1011	          // mid-build would wait an entire idle cycle to reach the
1012	          // client.
1013	          drainBufferedEvents();
1014	        } catch (e) {
1015	          console.error("SSE Poll Error", e);
1016	          const marker = recordSnapshotMarker(
1017	            getEventStreamNotificationVersion(),
1018	            runIdScope,
1019	          );
1020	          sendEvent("update_error", buildAppError(e, {
1021	            source: "Events",
1022	            action: "Stream live updates",
1023	          }), marker.streamId);
1024	          lastDeliveredId = marker.id;
1025	        }
1026	
1027	        if (!streamClosed) {

1029	          // cheap named frames immediately — transcript streaming keeps its

1031	          // and a wake caused only by delta-only events waits out the longer
1032	          // window instead of forcing a rebuild per streamed entry.
1033	          while (!streamClosed) {

1040	              // drift indefinitely, matching the previous behaviour.
1041	              emitStreamHeartbeatIfDue();
1042	              break;
1043	            }
1044	
1045	            const snapshotVersionNow = getEventStreamSnapshotVersion();
1046	            const hasSnapshotRelevantChange = snapshotVersionNow !== snapshotVersionAtLastBuild;
1047	            const requiredGapMs = hasSnapshotRelevantChange
1048	              ? MIN_SNAPSHOT_REBUILD_INTERVAL_MS
1049	              : DELTA_SNAPSHOT_REBUILD_INTERVAL_MS;

1053	            }

1056	            if (!streamClosed) {

1058	              drainBufferedEvents();
1059	            }

1061	          }
1062	        }
1063	      }
1064	      unsubscribeRevocation?.();
1065	      unsubscribeRevocation = null;
1066	    },
1067	    cancel() {
1068	      streamClosed = true;
1069	      unsubscribeRevocation?.();
1070	      unsubscribeRevocation = null;
1071	    },
1072	    onOverflow(overflow) {
1073	      streamClosed = true;
1074	      emitNamedEvent({
1075	        kind: "stream.subscriber_overflow",
1076	        stream: "events",
1077	        surface: context.surface,
1078	        ...overflow,
1079	        ...(runIdScope ? { runId: runIdScope } : {}),
1080	      });

1082	        kind: "error.surfaced",
1083	        code: "stream.subscriber_overflow",
1084	        message: "A slow event-stream subscriber exceeded its bounded queue and was disconnected.",

52	  status: text('status').notNull(), // 'idle', 'working', 'stuck', 'cred-exhausted'
53	  cwd: text('cwd').notNull(),

56	  allocationKey: text('allocation_key'),
57	  title: text('title').notNull().default(''),
58	  initialPrompt: text('initial_prompt').notNull().default(''),
59	  outputLog: text('output_log').notNull().default(''),
60	  outputEntriesJson: text('output_entries_json').notNull().default(''),
61	  currentText: text('current_text').notNull().default(''),
62	  lastText: text('last_text').notNull().default(''),

65	  effectiveLaunchModel: text('effective_launch_model'),
66	  effectiveLaunchEffort: text('effective_launch_effort'),
67	  launchCredentialSource: text('launch_credential_source'),
68	  // Monotonic fence advanced every time a turn is interrupted. A delivery
69	  // captures the generation it started under; stale completions from an
70	  // interrupted (older) turn compare their captured value and refuse to
71	  // persist terminal status/queue/response updates when it no longer matches.
72	  turnGeneration: integer('turn_generation').notNull().default(0),
73	  // Seq ranges this worker wrote for branches the user discarded via
74	  // retry/edit, as JSON `[{"from":n,"through":m}]`. A rewind to message M
75	  // supersedes everything from M's original delivery through the stream tip at
76	  // recovery time; the re-delivered message and its new answer land after that
77	  // (on a fresh worker, or further down this worker's stream when the ACP
78	  // session is resumed in place). Readers hide superseded entries so the
79	  // conversation shows one coherent thread instead of every abandoned attempt.
80	  supersededSeqRanges: text('superseded_seq_ranges'),

393	  const compressed = compressDiffContentPair(value);
394	  if (compressed) {
395	    // oldText/newText have already been compacted with diff-aware logic
396	    // that preserves their divergence. Skipping the generic per-string
397	    // truncator on those two fields is required — line-based truncation
398	    // would re-collapse them to identical head/tail strings and erase the
399	    // diff signal.
400	    return Object.fromEntries(
401	      Object.entries(compressed)
402	        .filter(([key]) => key !== "__diffCompressed")
403	        .map(([key, nested]) => (
404	          key === "oldText" || key === "newText"
405	            ? [key, nested]
406	            : [key, compactHistoryRawValue(nested)]
407	        )),
408	    );
409	  }
410	  return Object.fromEntries(
411	    Object.entries(value).map(([key, nested]) => [key, compactHistoryRawValue(nested)]),
412	  );
413	}
414	
415	type CompactableEntry = {
416	  type?: string;
417	  text?: string;
418	  raw?: unknown;
419	  [key: string]: unknown;
420	};
421	
422	export function compactEntryForHistory<T extends CompactableEntry>(entry: T): T {
423	  const text = (entry.type === "tool_call" || entry.type === "tool_call_update") && typeof entry.text === "string"
424	    ? truncateHistoryString(entry.text)
425	    : entry.text;
426	  if (entry.raw === undefined && text === entry.text) {
427	    return entry;
428	  }
429	  return {
430	    ...entry,
431	    text,
432	    raw: entry.raw === undefined ? undefined : compactHistoryRawValue(entry.raw),
433	  };
434	}
435	
436	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
437	// Per-worker write chain.
438	//
439	// Mutating operations on `${runId}/${workerId}` files acquire both an
440	// in-process chain and an OS-visible lock. The chain keeps local callers
441	// ordered; the file lock covers Next/server module instances and dev
442	// process boundaries. Bridge entry deduplication depends on this because
443	// every writer must re-read the current transcript before assigning seqs.
444	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
445	
446	const writeChainByKey = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
447	let tmpCounter = 0;
448	
449	// Cache of the next-seq to assign per (runId, workerId). Filled lazily on
450	// first append by reading existing entries. Kept valid by comparing file
451	// stat before each chained write so normal streaming appends do not parse
452	// the whole transcript every tick.
453	const nextSeqByKey = new Map<string, number>();
454	// Read-side cache: maps a (runId, workerId) to its latest persisted seq,
455	// pinned to the file's (size, mtimeMs). On a read we stat the file once;
456	// if the stat matches the pinned values, we return the cached seq without
457	// opening the file. Writes happen in a separate bridge process, so this
458	// cache cannot piggyback on nextSeqByKey — but the stat-based invariant
459	// catches any external writer's append correctly.
460	const readLatestSeqByKey = new Map<string, { latestSeq: number; size: number; mtimeMs: number }>();
461	// Same shape but for the full parsed entries list. Used by
462	// readWorkerEntriesSince to skip read+parse when (size, mtimeMs) matches.
463	// The entries list also lets us filter by afterSeq in memory, so even an
464	// afterSeq=0 first-load is served from this cache after the initial read.
465	const readEntriesByKey = new Map<string, { entries: WorkerEntry[]; latestSeq: number; size: number; mtimeMs: number }>();
466	// Cap how many full-entries chains we keep resident. Each value is the
467	// entire parsed transcript for one worker; with long-running supervisor
468	// runs across many workers this Map was the dominant resident-memory
469	// source. Map iteration order is insertion order, so we evict the
470	// oldest-inserted key on overflow. Cache hits also "touch" the key by
471	// re-inserting so genuinely-active chains stay resident.
472	const READ_ENTRIES_CACHE_MAX = 32;
473	function setReadEntriesCache(
474	  key: string,
475	  value: { entries: WorkerEntry[]; latestSeq: number; size: number; mtimeMs: number },
476	) {
477	  if (readEntriesByKey.has(key)) {
478	    readEntriesByKey.delete(key);
479	  } else if (readEntriesByKey.size >= READ_ENTRIES_CACHE_MAX) {
480	    const oldestKey = readEntriesByKey.keys().next().value;
481	    if (oldestKey !== undefined) readEntriesByKey.delete(oldestKey);
482	  }
483	  readEntriesByKey.set(key, value);
484	}
485	function touchReadEntriesCache(key: string) {
486	  const value = readEntriesByKey.get(key);
487	  if (value !== undefined) {
488	    readEntriesByKey.delete(key);
489	    readEntriesByKey.set(key, value);
490	  }
491	  return value;
492	}
493	// Cache of bridge entry ids that have already been written, used to make
494	// append-from-snapshot idempotent. Built lazily from the file on first
495	// use and updated on every successful append.
496	const seenIdsByKey = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
497	const fingerprintsByKey = new Map<string, Map<string, string>>();
498	const fileStateByKey = new Map<string, { size: number; mtimeMs: number }>();
499	let chainCacheDiskRefreshesForTests = 0;
500	
501	// Bound the write-side chain caches the same way as readEntriesByKey:
502	// supervisor runs can spawn hundreds of workers and seenIds/fingerprints
503	// each grow linearly with entry count per worker. Eviction is safe — the
504	// next refreshChainCaches call rebuilds from disk and from the DB-tracked
505	// latestSeq. Keep insertion order so cache hits "touch" by re-inserting.
506	const CHAIN_CACHE_MAX = 64;
507	function rememberChainKey(key: string) {
508	  // Insertion-order LRU across the four maps that share this key set.
509	  if (nextSeqByKey.has(key)) {
510	    nextSeqByKey.delete(key);
511	    seenIdsByKey.delete(key);
512	    fingerprintsByKey.delete(key);
513	    fileStateByKey.delete(key);
514	  } else if (nextSeqByKey.size >= CHAIN_CACHE_MAX) {
515	    const oldest = nextSeqByKey.keys().next().value;
516	    if (oldest !== undefined) {
517	      nextSeqByKey.delete(oldest);
518	      seenIdsByKey.delete(oldest);
519	      fingerprintsByKey.delete(oldest);
520	      fileStateByKey.delete(oldest);
521	    }
522	  }
523	}
524	
525	function chainKey(runId: string, workerId: string) {
526	  return `${runId}/${workerId}`;
527	}
528	
529	function runOnChain<T>(runId: string, workerId: string, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
530	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
531	  const previous = writeChainByKey.get(key) ?? Promise.resolve();
532	  const next = previous.then(() => task());
533	  const tracked = next.then(() => undefined, () => undefined);
534	  writeChainByKey.set(key, tracked);
535	  return next.finally(() => {
536	    if (writeChainByKey.get(key) === tracked) {
537	      writeChainByKey.delete(key);
538	    }
539	  });
540	}
541	
542	function clearChainCaches(runId: string, workerId: string) {
543	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
544	  nextSeqByKey.delete(key);
545	  seenIdsByKey.delete(key);
546	  fingerprintsByKey.delete(key);
547	  fileStateByKey.delete(key);
548	  readLatestSeqByKey.delete(key);
549	  readEntriesByKey.delete(key);
550	}
551	
552	function workerFileLockDelay(attempt: number) {
553	  const delay = WORKER_FILE_LOCK_MIN_TIMEOUT_MS * (WORKER_FILE_LOCK_FACTOR ** attempt);
554	  return Math.min(Math.round(delay), WORKER_FILE_LOCK_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS);
555	}
556	
557	function sleep(ms: number) {
558	  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
559	}
560	
561	function isRecoverableLockRaceError(error: unknown) {
562	  const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
563	  return code === "ENOENT" || code === "ENOTDIR" || code === "EINVAL";
564	}
565	
566	async function isWorkerFileLockStale(lockPath: string) {
567	  try {
568	    const stat = await fs.stat(lockPath);
569	    try {
570	      await fs.access(path.join(lockPath, "owner.json"));
571	    } catch (error) {
572	      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
573	        return true;
574	      }
575	      throw error;
576	    }
577	    return stat.mtimeMs < Date.now() - WORKER_FILE_LOCK_STALE_MS;
578	  } catch (error) {
579	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
580	      return true;
581	    }
582	    throw error;
583	  }
584	}
585	
586	async function acquireWorkerFileLock(lockPath: string): Promise<() => Promise<void>> {
587	  const ownerPath = path.join(lockPath, "owner.json");
588	  const ownerToken = randomUUID();
589	  const owner = JSON.stringify({
590	    token: [REDACTED]
591	    pid: process.pid,
592	    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
593	  });
594	
595	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= WORKER_FILE_LOCK_RETRIES; attempt += 1) {
596	    try {
597	      await fs.mkdir(lockPath);
598	      try {
599	        await fs.writeFile(ownerPath, owner, "utf8");
600	      } catch (error) {
601	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
602	        if (isRecoverableLockRaceError(error)) {
603	          continue;
604	        }
605	        throw error;
606	      }
607	
608	      let released = false;
609	      const refresh = async () => {
610	        if (released) {
611	          return;
612	        }
613	        const now = new Date();
614	        await fs.utimes(lockPath, now, now);
615	        await fs.utimes(ownerPath, now, now);
616	      };
617	      const interval = setInterval(() => {
618	        void refresh().catch(() => {});
619	      }, WORKER_FILE_LOCK_UPDATE_MS);
620	      interval.unref?.();
621	
622	      return async () => {
623	        if (released) {
624	          return;
625	        }
626	        released = true;
627	        clearInterval(interval);
628	        try {
629	          const currentOwner = await fs.readFile(ownerPath, "utf8");
630	          if (currentOwner !== owner) {
631	            return;
632	          }
633	        } catch (error) {
634	          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
635	            return;
636	          }
637	          throw error;
638	        }
639	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
640	      };
641	    } catch (error) {
642	      const code = (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
643	      if (code !== "EEXIST") {
644	        throw error;
645	      }
646	
647	      if (await isWorkerFileLockStale(lockPath)) {
648	        await fs.rm(lockPath, { recursive: true, force: true });
649	        continue;
650	      }
651	
652	      if (attempt === WORKER_FILE_LOCK_RETRIES) {
653	        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for worker output lock: ${lockPath}`), {
654	          code: "ELOCKED",
655	        });
656	      }
657	
658	      await sleep(workerFileLockDelay(attempt));
659	    }
660	  }
661	
662	  throw Object.assign(new Error(`Timed out waiting for worker output lock: ${lockPath}`), {
663	    code: "ELOCKED",
664	  });
665	}
666	
667	async function withWorkerFileLock<T>(
668	  runId: string,
669	  workerId: string,
670	  task: (paths: WorkerStreamPaths) => Promise<T>,
671	): Promise<T> {
672	  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "write");
673	  await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(paths.filePath), { recursive: true });
674	  // Appending an empty string with `a` is an atomic touch.
675	  await fs.writeFile(paths.filePath, "", { flag: "a" });
676	  const release = await acquireWorkerFileLock(paths.lockPath);
677	  try {
678	    return await task(paths);
679	  } finally {
680	    await release();
681	  }
682	}
683	
684	async function readWorkerFileState(runId: string, workerId: string) {
685	  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "read");
686	  try {
687	    const stat = await fs.stat(paths.filePath);
688	    return { size: stat.size, mtimeMs: stat.mtimeMs };
689	  } catch (error) {
690	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
691	      return { size: 0, mtimeMs: 0 };
692	    }
693	    throw error;
694	  }
695	}
696	
697	async function refreshChainCaches(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<{ nextSeq: number; seen: Set<string>; fingerprints: Map<string, string> }> {
698	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
699	  const currentFileState = await readWorkerFileState(runId, workerId);
700	  const cachedNextSeq = nextSeqByKey.get(key);
701	  const cachedSeen = seenIdsByKey.get(key);
702	  const cachedFingerprints = fingerprintsByKey.get(key);
703	  const cachedFileState = fileStateByKey.get(key);
704	  if (
705	    cachedNextSeq !== undefined
706	    && cachedSeen
707	    && cachedFingerprints
708	    && cachedFileState
709	    && cachedFileState.size === currentFileState.size
710	    && cachedFileState.mtimeMs === currentFileState.mtimeMs
711	  ) {
712	    // Touch the LRU so an actively-used chain stays resident.
713	    rememberChainKey(key);
714	    nextSeqByKey.set(key, cachedNextSeq);
715	    seenIdsByKey.set(key, cachedSeen);
716	    fingerprintsByKey.set(key, cachedFingerprints);
717	    fileStateByKey.set(key, cachedFileState);
718	    return {
719	      nextSeq: cachedNextSeq,
720	      seen: cachedSeen,
721	      fingerprints: cachedFingerprints,
722	    };
723	  }
724	
725	  chainCacheDiskRefreshesForTests += 1;
726	  // Use RAW persisted entries (pre-dedupe, pre-renumber) for the seq cursor
727	  // so we never advance backward. A previous in-disk corruption (e.g.
728	  // duplicate seqs from a cross-process race) used to be "corrected" by
729	  // normalizeWorkerEntrySeqs renumbering from 1, which then caused the
730	  // writer to land on seqs already present on disk — making the dupe
731	  // problem self-reinforcing. Read dedup signals (seen ids, fingerprints)
732	  // from the canonicalized view, but take maxSeq from the raw stream.
733	  const rawExisting = await readAllPersistedEntries(runId, workerId);
734	  let rawMaxSeq = 0;
735	  for (const entry of rawExisting) {
736	    if (typeof entry.seq === "number" && Number.isFinite(entry.seq) && entry.seq > rawMaxSeq) {
737	      rawMaxSeq = entry.seq;
738	    }
739	  }
740	  const canonical = normalizePersistedEntries(rawExisting);
741	  const seen = new Set<string>();
742	  const fingerprints = new Map<string, string>();
743	  for (const entry of canonical) {
744	    if (typeof entry.id === "string" && entry.id) {
745	      seen.add(entry.id);
746	      fingerprints.set(entry.id, workerEntryFingerprint(entry));
747	    }
748	  }
749	  // Cross-process safety: artifact_streams.latest_seq is updated after every
750	  // successful commit, so consulting it ensures we never reuse a seq another
751	  // process already claimed even if our file view is stale.
752	  let dbLatestSeq = 0;
753	  try {
754	    const { readArtifactStreamMetadata } = await import("@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata");
755	    const metadata = await readArtifactStreamMetadata({
756	      runId,
757	      kind: "worker_entries",
758	      ownerId: workerId,
759	    });
760	    if (metadata && typeof metadata.latestSeq === "number" && metadata.latestSeq > 0) {
761	      dbLatestSeq = metadata.latestSeq;
762	    }
763	  } catch {
764	    // Best-effort — if the metadata read fails, fall back to the file-only
765	    // cursor. The file lock still serializes within a process.
766	  }
767	  const nextSeq = Math.max(rawMaxSeq, dbLatestSeq) + 1;
768	  rememberChainKey(key);
769	  nextSeqByKey.set(key, nextSeq);
770	  seenIdsByKey.set(key, seen);
771	  fingerprintsByKey.set(key, fingerprints);
772	  fileStateByKey.set(key, await readWorkerFileState(runId, workerId));
773	  return { nextSeq, seen, fingerprints };
774	}
775	
776	async function rememberWorkerFileState(runId: string, workerId: string) {
777	  fileStateByKey.set(chainKey(runId, workerId), await readWorkerFileState(runId, workerId));
778	}
779	
780	async function readAllPersistedEntries(runId: string, workerId: string): Promise<WorkerEntry[]> {
781	  // Mirrors readWorkerOutputEntries's plaintext-first fallback chain but
782	  // returns the raw on-disk shape (WorkerEntry-ish — seq may be absent on
783	  // legacy lines; that's fine since the writer treats missing seq as 0).
784	  const paths = await workerStreamPaths(runId, workerId, "read");
785	  try {
786	    const body = await fs.readFile(paths.filePath, "utf8");
787	    const parsed = parseWorkerEntryLines(body);
788	    if (body.trim() || parsed.length > 0) {
789	      return parsed;
790	    }
791	  } catch (error) {
792	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") {
793	      throw error;
794	    }
795	  }
796	  const compressed = await readFromCompressedFile(paths.compressedFilePath);
797	  if (compressed.length > 0) {
798	    return compressed;
799	  }
800	  if (paths.filePath !== legacyWorkerFilePath(runId, workerId)) {
801	    const legacy = await readFromLegacyWorkerFiles(runId, workerId);
802	    if (legacy.length > 0) {
803	      return legacy;
804	    }
805	  }
806	  const archived = await readFromArchive(runId, workerId);
807	  if (archived.length > 0) {
808	    return archived;
809	  }
810	  return readLegacyDbEntries(workerId);
811	}
812	
813	/**
814	 * Guard against resuming a transcript mid-stream.
815	 *
816	 * `refreshChainCaches` seeds the seq cursor from
817	 * `max(fileMaxSeq, artifact_streams.latest_seq) + 1`. That `max()` exists for
818	 * cross-process safety, but it has a failure mode: when the plaintext stream
819	 * file is missing or empty while the DB cursor is already advanced, the writer
820	 * happily starts numbering at `latest_seq + 1` and appends forward forever. The
821	 * entries below that seq are never written, so the transcript silently loses its
822	 * head — the UI then renders the survivors as if the conversation began there.
823	 * This is what destroyed the head of runs e51514929b72 / e74cf7a81b7f /
824	 * ef23fac96fdb / 1795ba24270e.
825	 *
826	 * The fallback chain in `readAllPersistedEntries` can usually still see that
827	 * history (compacted `.gz`, the legacy path, or the raw runtime archive), but it
828	 * is only consulted while the plaintext is empty — the moment one entry lands,
829	 * the partial file shadows every fallback permanently. So the only safe moment
830	 * to repair is right here, before the first append.
831	 *
832	 * Must be called with the worker file lock held.
833	 */
834	async function healStrandedStreamHead(
835	  runId: string,
836	  workerId: string,
837	  paths: WorkerStreamPaths,
838	): Promise<void> {
839	  // Fast path: a non-empty file means the head (if any) is already
840	  // materialized. Normal streaming appends pay one stat and nothing else.
841	  // Stat `paths.filePath` (the write target) rather than going through
842	  // `readWorkerFileState`, whose read-mode resolution can point at the legacy
843	  // flat path and hide an empty live stream.
844	  const size = await fs.stat(paths.filePath).then((stat) => stat.size).catch(() => 0);
845	  if (size > 0) {
846	    return;
847	  }
848	
849	  let dbLatestSeq = 0;
850	  try {
851	    const { readArtifactStreamMetadata } = await import("@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata");
852	    const metadata = await readArtifactStreamMetadata({ runId, kind: "worker_entries", ownerId: workerId });
853	    if (metadata && typeof metadata.latestSeq === "number" && metadata.latestSeq > 0) {
854	      dbLatestSeq = metadata.latestSeq;
855	    }
856	  } catch {
857	    // Metadata unavailable — nothing to reconcile against, so nothing to heal.
858	    return;
859	  }
860	  if (dbLatestSeq <= 0) {
861	    // Genuinely a brand-new stream. Numbering starts at 1 as usual.
862	    return;
863	  }
864	
865	  // Empty file + advanced cursor = the head is stranded. Recover whatever the
866	  // fallback chain can still reach and write it back before numbering resumes.
867	  let recovered = await readAllPersistedEntries(runId, workerId);
868	  if (recovered.length === 0) {
869	    // Last resort: the agent runtime's raw output archive. It is the only
870	    // source that survived the outage this guard exists to prevent, and it is
871	    // deliberately NOT in readAllPersistedEntries's chain — `readFromArchive`
872	    // there reads the run `.zip`, a different artifact entirely.
873	    recovered = await readFromRuntimeOutputArchive(workerId);
874	  }
875	  if (recovered.length === 0) {
876	    emitNamedEvent({
877	      kind: "worker.stream_head_unrecoverable",
878	      runId,
879	      workerId,
880	      expectedLatestSeq: dbLatestSeq,
881	    });
882	    console.error(
883	      `[worker-output] ${workerId}: stream file is empty but artifact_streams.latest_seq=${dbLatestSeq}`
884	      + ` and no fallback source (gz/legacy/archive) holds the missing head.`
885	      + ` Resuming would strand ${dbLatestSeq} entries; resetting the cursor to 0 so numbering restarts at 1.`,
886	    );
887	    // Better to renumber from 1 than to leave a permanent unfillable hole.
888	    await setStreamCursor(runId, workerId, 0, null);
889	    return;
890	  }
891	
892	  const renumbered = recovered.map((entry, index) => {
893	    const { seq: _dropped, ...rest } = entry as WorkerEntry & { seq?: number };
894	    return compactEntryForHistory({ ...rest, seq: index + 1 } as unknown as CompactableEntry) as unknown as WorkerEntry;
895	  });
896	
897	  const body = renumbered.map((entry) => JSON.stringify(entry)).join("\n") + "\n";
898	  const tmpPath = `${paths.filePath}.heal-${process.pid}-${(tmpCounter += 1)}.tmp`;
899	  const handle = await fs.open(tmpPath, "w");
900	  try {
901	    await handle.writeFile(body, "utf8");
902	    await handle.sync();
903	  } finally {
904	    await handle.close();
905	  }
906	  await fs.rename(tmpPath, paths.filePath);
907	
908	  // Set the cursor directly: the recovered transcript is authoritative, and it
909	  // is usually SHORTER than the stale cursor (streaming chunks collapse into
910	  // assembled entries). `commitArtifactAppend` never moves a cursor backward,
911	  // so using it here would leave the writer numbering above the file again.
912	  const last = renumbered.at(-1);
913	  await setStreamCursor(runId, workerId, renumbered.length, last?.id ?? `seq-${renumbered.length}`);
914	
915	  // Force the next refreshChainCaches to re-read from the healed file.
916	  const key = chainKey(runId, workerId);
917	  nextSeqByKey.delete(key);
918	  seenIdsByKey.delete(key);
919	  fingerprintsByKey.delete(key);
920	  fileStateByKey.delete(key);
921	
922	  emitNamedEvent({
923	    kind: "worker.stream_head_healed",
924	    runId,
925	    workerId,
926	    expectedLatestSeq: dbLatestSeq,
927	    recoveredEntries: renumbered.length,
928	  });
929	  console.warn(
930	    `[worker-output] ${workerId}: recovered ${renumbered.length} stranded entries into an empty stream file`
931	    + ` (cursor was at ${dbLatestSeq}); transcript head preserved.`,
932	  );
933	}
934	
935	/**
936	 * Read the agent runtime's raw output archive for a worker and reassemble it
937	 * into worker-stream shape.
938	 *
939	 * The runtime writes every bridge record here as it streams, so this file
940	 * outlives stream-file damage. Its records are per-chunk, so streaming deltas
941	 * must be re-joined (see `reassembleArchivedEntries`) or the transcript comes
942	 * back shredded mid-word.
943	 */
944	async function readFromRuntimeOutputArchive(workerId: string): Promise<WorkerEntry[]> {
945	  const archivePath = path.join(
946	    process.cwd(),
947	    ".omniharness",
948	    "agent-runtime-output",
949	    `${workerId}.jsonl`,
950	  );
951	  let body: string;
952	  try {
953	    body = await fs.readFile(archivePath, "utf8");
954	  } catch {
955	    return [];
956	  }
957	  const parsed = parseWorkerEntryLines(body).filter((entry) => entry.id !== "output-archive-marker");
958	  if (parsed.length === 0) {

84	export interface SidebarActivityIndex {

91	export function buildSidebarActivityIndex(args: {
92	  messages: MessageInput[];
93	  queuedMessages: QueuedMessageInput[];
94	  workers: WorkerInput[];

96	}): SidebarActivityIndex {
97	  const latestMessageAtByRunId = new Map<string, string>();
98	  const latestUserInputAtByRunId = new Map<string, string>();
99	  const workersByRunId = new Map<string, WorkerInput[]>();
100	  const agentsByWorkerId = new Map<string, AgentInput>();
101	
102	  const keepLater = (map: Map<string, string>, runId: string, value: string | null | undefined) => {
103	    if (!value) return;
104	    const existing = map.get(runId);
105	    if (!existing || parseTimestampMs(value) > parseTimestampMs(existing)) {
106	      map.set(runId, value);
107	    }
108	  };
109	
110	  for (const message of args.messages) {
111	    keepLater(latestMessageAtByRunId, message.runId, message.createdAt);
112	    if (isUserInputMessage(message)) {
113	      keepLater(latestUserInputAtByRunId, message.runId, message.createdAt);
114	    }
115	  }
116	
117	  for (const queued of args.queuedMessages) {
118	    keepLater(
119	      latestUserInputAtByRunId,
120	      queued.runId,
121	      queued.deliveredAt ?? queued.updatedAt ?? queued.createdAt,
122	    );
123	  }
124	
125	  for (const worker of args.workers) {
126	    const bucket = workersByRunId.get(worker.runId);
127	    if (bucket) {
128	      bucket.push(worker);
129	    } else {
130	      workersByRunId.set(worker.runId, [worker]);
131	    }

134	  for (const agent of args.agents) {
135	    agentsByWorkerId.set(agent.name, agent);
136	  }
137	
138	  return { latestMessageAtByRunId, latestUserInputAtByRunId, workersByRunId, agentsByWorkerId };
139	}

216	function isIndexedSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking(run: RunInput, index: SidebarActivityIndex): boolean {
217	  // Terminal runs are never "working" — stale worker metadata loses.
218	  if (isTerminalRunStatus(run.status)) return false;
219	
220	  const normalizedStatus = normalizeRunStatus(run.status);
221	  if (normalizedStatus === "needs_recovery") return false;
222	
223	  if (normalizedStatus !== "running" && normalizedStatus !== "awaiting_user") return false;

229	    const agent = index.agentsByWorkerId.get(worker.id);
230	    if (agent && isWorkerActiveStatus(agent.state)) return true;
231	  }
232	
233	  // Run is "running" with no active workers/agents yet — still counts.
234	  return normalizedStatus === "running";
235	}

250	/**

255	export function classifyIndexedSidebarRun(
256	  args: Pick<SidebarRunActivityArgs, "run" | "readMarkers" | "workerOutputObservedAtByRunId" | "nowMs" | "selectedRunId">,
257	  index: SidebarActivityIndex,
258	): RunActiveClassification {
259	  const { run, readMarkers, nowMs } = args;
260	  const lastReadAt = readMarkers[run.id] ?? null;
261	  const normalizedStatus = normalizeRunStatus(run.status);
262	
263	  const latestUnreadAt = getIndexedRunLatestUnreadTimestamp(run, index);
264	  const isUnread = isRunUnread({ latestMessageAt: latestUnreadAt, lastReadAt });
265	
266	  const isWorking = isIndexedSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking(run, index);
267	
268	  const recentActivityAt = getIndexedSidebarRunLastActivityAt(args, index);
269	  const allowsRecentActivity = normalizedStatus !== "cancelled" && normalizedStatus !== "canceled";
270	  const isRecent =
271	    allowsRecentActivity &&
272	    recentActivityAt !== null &&
273	    nowMs - parseTimestampMs(recentActivityAt) <= ACTIVE_SESSION_ACTIVITY_WINDOW_MS;
274	
275	  const isSelected = args.selectedRunId != null && args.run.id === args.selectedRunId;
276	  const isActive = isUnread || isWorking || isRecent || isSelected;
277	
278	  let activeSortAt: string | null = recentActivityAt;
279	  if (isUnread && latestUnreadAt) {
280	    activeSortAt = maxTimestamp(activeSortAt, latestUnreadAt);
281	  }
282	  if (isWorking) {
283	    activeSortAt = maxTimestamp(activeSortAt, getIndexedWorkingActivityAt(run, index));
284	  }
285	  if (!activeSortAt) activeSortAt = run.createdAt;
286	
287	  return { isActive, isUnread, isWorking, isRecent, recentActivityAt, activeSortAt };
288	}

290	export function compareActiveSidebarRunsDesc(
291	  a: { activeSortAt: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
292	  b: { activeSortAt: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
293	): number {
294	  const diff = parseTimestampMs(b.activeSortAt) - parseTimestampMs(a.activeSortAt);
295	  if (diff !== 0) return diff;
296	  const createdDiff = parseTimestampMs(b.createdAt) - parseTimestampMs(a.createdAt);
297	  if (createdDiff !== 0) return createdDiff;
298	  return a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0;
299	}

333	        },

340	      if (!result.isActive) continue;

1	// Non-persistent live worker-output observation timestamps derived from
2	// worker-entry cursor increases. Only seq increases after the initial baseline
3	// are counted as recent activity; historical entries never make a run look active.
4	
5	export interface SidebarWorkerObservation {
6	  runId: string | null;
7	  seq: number;
8	  observedAt: string;
9	}
10	
11	export class SidebarWorkerActivityManager {
12	  // Baseline seqs from the initial snapshot; these are NOT counted as recent.
13	  private readonly baselineSeqs = new Map<string, number>();
14	  // Live observations: workerId -> { runId, seq, observedAt }
15	  private readonly observations = new Map<string, SidebarWorkerObservation>();
16	  // Derived view: runId -> latest observed worker-output timestamp
17	  private readonly runOutputAt = new Map<string, string>();
18	
19	  // Called with workerEntrySeqs from every snapshot/update to establish baselines.
20	  // Does NOT record an observation — only sets the floor for future seq comparisons.
21	  onKnownSeqs(seqs: Record<string, number> | undefined): void {
22	    if (!seqs) return;
23	    for (const [workerId, seq] of Object.entries(seqs)) {
24	      if (typeof seq !== "number") continue;
25	      // Set baseline only if we have not yet seen a live increase for this worker.
26	      if (!this.observations.has(workerId) && !this.baselineSeqs.has(workerId)) {
27	        this.baselineSeqs.set(workerId, seq);
28	      }
29	    }
30	  }
31	
32	  // Called when a worker.entry_appended SSE frame arrives.
33	  // Only records an observation when seq strictly exceeds the known baseline.
34	  onWakeUp(args: { workerId: string; seq: number; runId?: string | null }): void {
35	    const { workerId, seq, runId } = args;
36	    const baseline = this.baselineSeqs.get(workerId);
37	
38	    if (baseline === undefined) {
39	      // First time seeing this worker — treat this as the baseline.
40	      this.baselineSeqs.set(workerId, seq);
41	      return;
42	    }
43	
44	    if (seq <= baseline) {
45	      // Not a new entry after page load; ignore.
46	      return;
47	    }
48	
49	    const existing = this.observations.get(workerId);
50	    if (existing && existing.seq >= seq) {
51	      // No-op: already recorded this seq or a later one.
52	      return;
53	    }
54	
55	    const observedAt = new Date().toISOString();
56	    const resolvedRunId = runId ?? existing?.runId ?? null;
57	
58	    this.observations.set(workerId, { runId: resolvedRunId, seq, observedAt });
59	
60	    if (resolvedRunId) {
61	      const current = this.runOutputAt.get(resolvedRunId);
62	      if (!current || new Date(observedAt).getTime() > new Date(current).getTime()) {
63	        this.runOutputAt.set(resolvedRunId, observedAt);
64	      }
65	    }
66	  }
67	
68	  getRunOutputAt(runId: string): string | null {
69	    return this.runOutputAt.get(runId) ?? null;
70	  }
71	
72	  getRunOutputAtRecord(): Record<string, string> {
73	    return Object.fromEntries(this.runOutputAt);
74	  }
75	}

23	export async function persistRunFailure(
24	  runId: string,
25	  error: unknown,
26	  options: PersistRunFailureOptions = {},
27	) {
28	  const errorMessage = formatErrorMessage(error);
29	  const now = new Date();
30	  const content = `Run failed: ${errorMessage}`;
31	  const currentRun = await db.select().from(runs).where(eq(runs.id, runId)).get();
32	  if (!currentRun || (isTerminalRunStatus(currentRun.status) && normalizeRunStatus(currentRun.status) !== "failed")) {
33	    return;
34	  }
35	
36	  const previousStatus = normalizeRunStatus(currentRun.status);
37	  const isFirstTransitionToFailed = previousStatus !== "failed";
38	  if (!isFirstTransitionToFailed && currentRun.lastError === errorMessage) {
39	    return;
40	  }
41	
42	  await db.update(runs).set({
43	    status: "failed",
44	    failedAt: now,
45	    lastError: errorMessage,
46	    updatedAt: now,
47	  }).where(eq(runs.id, runId));
48	  notifyEventStreamSubscribers();
49	
50	  // Emit error.surfaced once, on the actual transition into the failed
51	  // state. Skip re-emission on duplicate calls so retries / fall-through
52	  // safety nets don't double-toast the user.
53	  if (options.surface && isFirstTransitionToFailed) {
54	    const cause = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(errorMessage);
55	    emitNamedEvent({
56	      kind: "error.surfaced",
57	      code: options.surface.code,
58	      message: errorMessage,
59	      surface: options.surface.surface ?? "toast",
60	      runId,
61	      ...(options.surface.workerId ? { workerId: options.surface.workerId } : {}),
62	      cause: { name: cause.name, message: cause.message },
63	    });
64	  }
65	
66	  const latestMessage = await db.select().from(messages)
67	    .where(eq(messages.runId, runId))
68	    .orderBy(desc(messages.createdAt), desc(messages.id))
69	    .get();
70	
71	  if (
72	    latestMessage?.role === "system"
73	    && latestMessage.kind === "error"
74	    && latestMessage.content === content
75	  ) {
76	    return;
77	  }
78	
79	  const workerId = options.surface?.workerId ?? null;
80	  const eventWorkerId = workerId
81	    ? (await db.select({ id: workers.id }).from(workers).where(eq(workers.id, workerId)).get())?.id ?? null
82	    : null;
83	  await recordExecutionEvent({
84	    runId,
85	    workerId: eventWorkerId,
86	    eventType: "run_failed",
87	    details: {

89	      error: errorMessage,
90	      code: options.surface?.code ?? null,
91	      surface: options.surface?.surface ?? null,
92	    },
93	    createdAt: now,
94	  });

98	    runId,
99	    role: "system",
100	    kind: "error",
101	    content,
102	    createdAt: now,
103	  });

## Summary of Database Message Persistence Investigation

Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here are the findings:

### 1. **All 18 places where `db.insert(messages)` is called:**

| File | Line | Role | Kind | Trigger |
|------|------|------|------|---------|

| `/src/server/conversations/queued-message-interrupt.ts` | 429 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Delivering queued steer message to worker |
| `/src/server/conversations/send-message.ts` | 194 | `user` | `elicitation` | Answering worker elicitation in direct runs |
| `/src/server/conversations/send-message.ts` | 1129 | `user` | `checkpoint` or `clarification_answer` | Sending user reply to checkpoint in pending run |
| `/src/server/conversations/send-message.ts` | 1233 | `user` | `checkpoint` | User sending message to active worker |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 947 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Dequeuing pending message for supervised run |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1094 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Delivering queued answer to worker question |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1095 | `supervisor` | `update` | Confirmation response after queued message delivery |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1166 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Draining recovered human input entries |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1283 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Delivering queued answer to direct worker elicitation |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1328 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Delivering queued planning turn input |
| `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts` | 1371 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Delivering queued message for planning run |
| `/src/server/runs/failures.ts` | 96 | `system` | `error` | Run failure (error message logged) |
| `/src/server/runs/recovery.ts` | 1145 | (various) | `checkpoint` or original `kind` | Forking a run (copies messages up to fork point) |
| `/src/server/runs/recovery-actions.ts` | 67 | `user` | `checkpoint` | Draining pending queued messages on recovery |

### 2. **Worker turn output persistence:**

**Worker response text is NOT persisted in the `messages` table.** Instead:

- Worker final assistant text is written to the **unified worker stream** (JSONL entries in `artifact_streams` with `kind='worker_entries'`)
- These entries are persisted **incrementally as they stream** via `appendWorkerEntryWithResult()` and `writeWorkerOutputEntries()` in `/src/server/workers/output-store.ts`
- The stream file is stored at: `.omniharness/artifacts/runs/{runId}/workers/{workerId}.jsonl`
- Comments at:
  - `/src/server/conversations/send-message.ts:1102-1103`: "Worker response now lives in the unified worker stream — the bridge entries written by persistWorkerSnapshot above carry the response text. The legacy role:"worker" messages row is gone."
  - `/src/server/conversations/queued-messages.ts:1163-1164`: "Worker response now lives in the unified worker stream; the legacy role:"worker" messages row is no longer written."

### 3. **Conversation UI rendering:**

The UI reads worker turns from **two different sources**:

1. **For direct/planning runs**: Worker output lives in the worker stream (`workerEntries`), NOT in `messages` table
2. **For queued messages**: After delivery, only the `user` message enters the `messages` table; the supervisor sends a separate `role:supervisor` confirmation message
3. The conversation view reconstructs the full turn from: user message (in `messages`) + worker output entries (from `artifact_streams`)

See `/src/server/conversations/create.ts` and `/src/server/conversations/send-message.ts` for the worker-stream-first architecture.

### 4. **`workerOutputObservedAtByRunId` - Client-only ephemeral state:**

**Location:** `/src/interface/home/SidebarWorkerActivityManager.ts`

**Nature:** Purely **client-only, ephemeral state** — **NOT persisted to database**

**How it works:**
- `SidebarWorkerActivityManager` maintains in-memory maps (lines 13-17):
  - `baselineSeqs`: Worker entry seq at initial snapshot (NOT an observation)
  - `observations`: Live worker-entry appends after page load
  - `runOutputAt`: Derived map from runId → latest observed timestamp
- `onWakeUp()` (line 34) records an observation only when `seq > baseline` (new entries after page load)
- `observedAt` is captured as `new Date().toISOString()` at observation time (line 55)
- `getRunOutputAtRecord()` (line 72) returns only in-memory entries

**Key insight:** This timestamp is used for the sidebar's "recent activity" classification but **has no DB persistence**. On page reload, the baselines reset and only seq increases from the initial snapshot onwards count as "activity." This explains why historical worker output never makes a run look "active" in the sidebar.

**Files using it:**
- `/src/interface/home/useHomeViewModel.ts:217` - reads it via `sidebarWorkerActivityManager.getRunOutputAtRecord()`
- `/src/interface/home/sidebar-activity.ts:168,183` - uses it in activity classification logic

## Summary of Findings

### 1. How `messageRunIds` / `messageScope` is Computed

**In `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:293-304`:**
```typescript
function selectedMessageRunIds(records: PersistedEventRecords, options: EventPayloadOptions) {
  const selectedRunId = resolveVisibleSelectedRunId(records, options);
  if (!selectedRunId) {
    return [];
  }

  const selectedRun = records.allRuns.find((run) => run.id === selectedRunId);
  return [
    ...(selectedRun?.mode === "implementation" && selectedRun.parentRunId ? [selectedRun.parentRunId] : []),
    selectedRunId,
  ];
}
```

**In `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:127-129`:**
```typescript
selectedRunId
  ? db.select().from(messages).where(inArray(messages.runId, transcriptRunIds)).orderBy(asc(messages.createdAt), asc(messages.id))
  : [],
```

**In `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/events/persisted-snapshot.ts:264-266`:**
```typescript
selectedRunId
  ? db.select().from(messages).where(inArray(messages.runId, transcriptRunIds)).orderBy(asc(messages.createdAt), asc(messages.id))
  : [],
```

**Answer: Messages are loaded ONLY for a scoped subset of runs.** When no `selectedRunId` is provided, `[]` (empty array) is returned. When a run IS selected:
- If the run is in "implementation" mode with a `parentRunId`, messages are loaded for **both** the parent run and the selected run
- Otherwise, messages are loaded **only** for the selected run

The `messageScope` returned in the payload (`src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:541-544` and `src/server/events/persisted-snapshot.ts:361-364`) contains:
```typescript
messageScope: {
  runIds: messageRunIds,  // or transcriptRunIds in persisted-snapshot
  complete: true,
}
```

---

### 2. Per-Run Message Time Aggregates

**No SQL aggregates are computed server-side.** The code loads ALL messages for the selected run(s) with no `max(created_at)` grouping. The full message history is fetched and serialized in memory.

---

### 3. SQL Indexes on Messages

**In `/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/db/index.ts:837-838`:**
```sql
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS messages_run_created_idx ON messages(run_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS messages_run_created_id_idx ON messages(run_id, created_at, id);
```

Both indexes exist and support:
- Filtering by `run_id` + `created_at` (exact order used in the query)
- Prefix query on `(run_id, created_at, id)` for stable ordering with ties

**Note:** There is **no index on `messages(run_id, created_at DESC)`**, so descending queries would need to reverse-scan.

### Assessment of `runs.updatedAt` Fidelity

**`runs.updatedAt` is NOT a reliable "last user message or last finished agent turn" proxy.** It gets bumped by:

1. **Bookkeeping operations (high volume):**

   - Runtime watchdog recovery actions (health checks)
   - Git auto-commit (completion marker)
   - Recovery reconciliation (background fault tolerance)

3. **Process session status changes** (for process-mode runs only)

**Reliable indicators:**
- `messages.createdAt` for the last user message timestamp
- `messages.createdAt` (role='user') for last user interaction
- `runs.status` combined with message timestamps for inference
- `clarifications.status` for awaiting-user states

**Unreliable for "last meaningful activity":**
- `runs.updatedAt` alone — will reflect background bookkeeping
- Needs to be paired with message timestamps or status inference

65	async function fetchWithTimeout(url: string, timeoutMs: number) {
66	  const controller = new AbortController();
67	  let timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
68	
69	  try {
70	    return await Promise.race([
71	      fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }),
72	      new Promise<Response>((_, reject) => {
73	        timeout = setTimeout(() => {
74	          controller.abort();
75	          reject(new Error(`Agent runtime list request timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms.`));
76	        }, timeoutMs);
77	      }),
78	    ]);
79	  } finally {
80	    if (timeout) {
81	      clearTimeout(timeout);
82	    }
83	  }
84	}

313	function compactExecutionEventDetails(details: string | null) {
314	  if (!details?.trim()) {
315	    return details ?? null;
316	  }
317	
318	  try {
319	    const parsed = JSON.parse(details) as Record<string, unknown>;
320	    const compacted: Record<string, unknown> = {};
321	
322	    for (const key of [
323	      "summary",
324	      "reason",
325	      "error",
326	      "mode",
327	      "seconds",
328	      "recoveryState",
329	      "recommendedAction",
330	      "resetAt",
331	      "resumeAt",
332	      "scheduledWakeAt",
333	      "quotaResetSource",
334	      "quotaResetConfidence",
335	      "retryAfterMs",
336	      "provider",
337	      "sourceType",
338	      "rawText",
339	    ]) {
340	      const value = parsed[key];
341	      if (typeof value === "string") {
342	        compacted[key] = truncateText(value, EXECUTION_EVENT_DETAIL_LIMIT);
343	      } else if (typeof value === "number") {
344	        compacted[key] = value;
345	      }
346	    }
347	
348	    return Object.keys(compacted).length > 0 ? JSON.stringify(compacted) : "{}";
349	  } catch {
350	    return JSON.stringify({
351	      summary: truncateText(details, EXECUTION_EVENT_DETAIL_LIMIT),
352	    });
353	  }
354	}

389	function deriveRecoveryState(incidents: PersistedEventRecords["allRecoveryIncidents"]) {
390	  const active = incidents.find((incident) => (
391	    incident.status === "open"
392	    || incident.status === "recovering"
393	    || incident.status === "needs_user"
394	    || incident.status === "failed"
395	  ));
396	  if (!active) {
397	    return null;
398	  }
399	
400	  let parsedDetails: Record<string, unknown> = {};
401	  try {
402	    parsedDetails = active.details ? JSON.parse(active.details) as Record<string, unknown> : {};
403	  } catch {
404	    parsedDetails = {};
405	  }
406	
407	  return {
408	    kind: String(parsedDetails.recoveryState ?? active.kind),
409	    status: active.status,
410	    workerId: active.workerId,
411	    queuedMessageId: active.queuedMessageId,
412	    message: typeof parsedDetails.reason === "string" ? parsedDetails.reason : active.lastError,
413	    recommendedAction: String(parsedDetails.recommendedAction ?? (
414	      active.status === "recovering" ? "none" : "manual_resume"
415	    )),
416	    lastError: active.lastError,
417	    attemptCount: active.autoAttemptCount,
418	    nextAttemptAt: typeof parsedDetails.nextAttemptAt === "string" ? parsedDetails.nextAttemptAt : null,
419	    resumeAt: typeof parsedDetails.resumeAt === "string" ? parsedDetails.resumeAt : null,

421	    quotaResetConfidence: typeof parsedDetails.quotaResetConfidence === "string" ? parsedDetails.quotaResetConfidence : null,

426	function compactAgentSnapshot(agent: ReturnType<typeof buildLiveWorkerSnapshots>[number]) {
427	  // Worker conversation content (outputEntries) is no longer carried
428	  // on the /api/events snapshot. Clients fetch it via
429	  // /api/workers/:workerId/entries through `WorkerEntriesManager`. The
430	  // agents[] array stays for non-content metadata: state, the
431	  // "thinking…" indicator, bridge-missing flag, last error.
432	  return {
433	    ...agent,
434	    outputEntries: [],
435	    renderedOutput: null,
436	    currentText: truncateText(agent.currentText, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
437	    lastText: truncateText(agent.lastText, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
438	    outputLog: truncateText(agent.outputLog, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
439	    displayText: truncateText(agent.displayText, AGENT_TEXT_FIELD_LIMIT),
440	    stderrBuffer: (agent.stderrBuffer ?? []).slice(-10).map((line) => truncateText(line, 2_000)),
441	  };
442	}

444	async function buildWorkerEntrySeqs(workers: Array<{ id: string; runId: string }>) {
445	  const seqs = await Promise.all(
446	    workers.map(async (worker) => {
447	      const seq = await readWorkerLatestSeq(worker.runId, worker.id);
448	      return seq > 0 ? [worker.id, seq] as const : null;
449	    }),
450	  );
451	  return Object.fromEntries(seqs.filter((seq): seq is readonly [string, number] => Boolean(seq)));
452	}

454	function filterRuntimeAgentsForWorkers(rawAgents: unknown[], scopedWorkers: PersistedEventRecords["allWorkers"]) {
455	  const workerIds = new Set(scopedWorkers.map((worker) => worker.id));
456	  if (workerIds.size === 0) {
457	    return [];
458	  }
459	
460	  return rawAgents.filter((agent) => {
461	    if (typeof agent !== "object" || agent === null) {
462	      return false;
463	    }
464	
465	    const name = (agent as { name?: unknown }).name;
466	    return typeof name === "string" && workerIds.has(name);
467	  });
468	}

470	function buildEventPayload(
471	  records: PersistedEventRecords,
472	  agentsData: ReturnType<typeof buildLiveWorkerSnapshots>,
473	  frontendErrors: AppErrorPayload[] = [],
474	  options: EventPayloadOptions = {},
475	  workerEntrySeqs: Record<string, number> = {},
476	  claudeModelGateway = getClaudeModelGatewayService().getSnapshot(),
477	) {
478	  const selectedRunId = resolveVisibleSelectedRunId(records, options);
479	  const runIds = visibleSelectedRunIds(records, options);
480	  const messageRunIds = selectedMessageRunIds(records, options);
481	  const lifecycleErrors = buildAwaitingUserQuestionInvariantErrors({
482	    runs: records.allRuns,
483	    messages: records.msgs,
484	    clarifications: records.allClarifications,
485	    selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
486	  });
487	  const processSessionsByRunId = new Map<string, PersistedEventRecords["allProcessSessions"][number]>(
488	    records.allProcessSessions.map((session) => [session.runId, session]),
489	  );
490	  const workersByRunId = new Map<string, PersistedEventRecords["allWorkers"][number]>();
491	  for (const worker of records.allWorkers) {
492	    if (!workersByRunId.has(worker.runId)) {
493	      workersByRunId.set(worker.runId, worker);
494	    }
495	  }
496	  const sessions = records.allRuns.map((run) => serializeSessionRecord({
497	    run,
498	    primaryWorker: workersByRunId.get(run.id) ?? null,
499	    processSession: processSessionsByRunId.get(run.id) ?? null,
500	  }));
501	  const readMarkers = Object.fromEntries(
502	    records.allReadMarkers.map((marker) => [marker.runId, marker.lastReadAt.toISOString()]),
503	  );
504	  // Worker conversation content now lives in the unified worker stream
505	  // (per-worker JSONL, fetched via /api/workers/:workerId/entries). The
506	  // previous `synthesizeStreamingWorkerMessages` path that fabricated
507	  // pseudo-messages from `agent.outputEntries` is gone; clients render
508	  // worker content via `WorkerEntriesManager` instead.
509	  return withEventPayloadChecksum({
510	    messages: records.msgs.map(serializeMessageRecord),
511	    readMarkers,
512	    plans: records.allPlans,
513	    runs: records.allRuns.map((run) => stripUnusedRunSnapshotFields(run, { selectedRunId })),
514	    sessions,
515	    accounts: records.allAccounts.map(toAccountDto),
516	    agents: agentsData.map(compactAgentSnapshot),
517	    workers: records.allWorkers.map(compactWorkerRecord),
518	    planItems: records.allPlanItems,
519	    clarifications: records.allClarifications,
520	    executionEvents: records.allExecutionEvents
521	      .slice(0, EXECUTION_EVENT_LIMIT)
522	      .map(compactExecutionEvent),
523	    supervisorInterventions: records.allSupervisorInterventions
524	      .map(compactSupervisorIntervention),
525	    queuedMessages: records.allQueuedMessages
526	      .filter((message) => message.status === "pending" || message.status === "delivering")
527	      .map(serializeQueuedConversationMessage),
528	    recoveryIncidents: records.allRecoveryIncidents
529	      .map(compactRecoveryIncident),

581	async function buildPersistedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {

583	  probe?.mark("readRecords.total");
584	  const scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
585	  const workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
586	  probe?.mark(`workerSeqs[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);

594	    options,

596	  );

601	type EventPayloadCacheEntry = {
602	  version: number;
603	  promise: Promise<EventPayload>;
604	};

606	const cachedPersistedPayloads = new Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>();
607	const cachedRuntimePayloads = new Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>();

609	export function __clearEventPayloadCachesForTests() {
610	  cachedPersistedPayloads.clear();
611	  cachedRuntimePayloads.clear();

614	function eventPayloadCacheKey(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}) {
615	  return options.selectedRunId?.trim() || "__all__";
616	}
617	
618	function shareInFlightEventPayload(
619	  cache: Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>,
620	  options: EventPayloadOptions,
621	  build: () => Promise<EventPayload>,
622	) {
623	  const key = eventPayloadCacheKey(options);
624	  const version = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
625	  const existing = cache.get(key);
626	  if (existing?.version === version) {
627	    return existing.promise;
628	  }
629	
630	  const pending = build().catch((error) => {
631	    const cached = cache.get(key);
632	    if (cached?.promise === pending) {
633	      cache.delete(key);
634	    }
635	    throw error;
636	  });
637	  cache.set(key, { version, promise: pending });
638	  pruneEventPayloadCache(cache);
639	  return pending;
640	}
641	
642	function pruneEventPayloadCache(cache: Map<string, EventPayloadCacheEntry>) {
643	  while (cache.size > EVENT_PAYLOAD_CACHE_LIMIT) {
644	    const oldestKey = cache.keys().next().value;
645	    if (!oldestKey) {
646	      return;
647	    }
648	    cache.delete(oldestKey);
649	  }
650	}

660	async function buildRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(options: EventPayloadOptions = {}, probe?: { mark: (label: string) => void }) {
661	  let records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options, probe);
662	  probe?.mark("readRecords#1.total");
663	  let scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
664	  let workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
665	  probe?.mark(`workerSeqs#1[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
666	  let agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
667	    workers: scopedWorkers,
668	    runs: records.allRuns,
669	  });
670	  const frontendErrors: AppErrorPayload[] = [];
671	
672	  try {
673	    const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`${BRIDGE_URL}/agents`, RUNTIME_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS);
674	    probe?.mark("bridge.fetch");
675	    if (res.ok) {
676	      const rawAgentsPayload = await res.json();
677	      const rawAgents = Array.isArray(rawAgentsPayload) ? rawAgentsPayload : [];
678	      const { syncConversationSessions } = await import("@/server/conversations/sync");
679	      await syncConversationSessions(rawAgents, {
680	        selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
681	        refreshPlanningArtifacts: false,
682	      });
683	      probe?.mark("bridge.sync");
684	      // Second reconciliation pass — this one knows what's actually in
685	      // the bridge, so it can detect workers that were "working" when
686	      // the bridge died and are now stranded with no live agent. The
687	      // earlier pass (inside readPersistedEventRecords) couldn't see
688	      // this because it ran before we fetched the bridge agent list.
689	      const bridgeAgentNames = new Set<string>();
690	      for (const agent of rawAgents) {
691	        if (typeof agent === "object" && agent !== null) {
692	          const name = (agent as { name?: unknown }).name;
693	          if (typeof name === "string" && name.length > 0) {
694	            bridgeAgentNames.add(name);
695	          }
696	        }
697	      }
698	      await reconcilePersistedReloadZombies({
699	        selectedRunId: options.selectedRunId,
700	        source: "events-snapshot-post-bridge",
701	        bridgeAgentNames,
702	      });
703	      probe?.mark("reconcile.bridge-orphans");
704	      records = await readPersistedEventRecords(options);
705	      probe?.mark("readRecords#2.total");
706	      scopedWorkers = selectedRunWorkers(records, options);
707	      workerEntrySeqs = await buildWorkerEntrySeqs(scopedWorkers);
708	      probe?.mark(`workerSeqs#2[${scopedWorkers.length}]`);
709	      agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
710	        agents: filterRuntimeAgentsForWorkers(rawAgents, scopedWorkers),
711	        workers: scopedWorkers,
712	        runs: records.allRuns,
713	      });
714	    } else {
715	      const bridgeError = new Error(`Agent runtime list request failed with status ${res.status}.`);
716	      agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
717	        workers: scopedWorkers,
718	        runs: records.allRuns,
719	        bridgeError,
720	      });
721	      if (!isTransientSupervisorError(bridgeError)) {
722	        frontendErrors.push(buildAppError(
723	          bridgeError,
724	          {
725	            source: "Agent runtime",
726	            action: "Stream live agent state",
727	          },
728	        ));
729	      }
730	    }
731	  } catch (error) {
732	    agentsData = buildLiveWorkerSnapshots({
733	      workers: scopedWorkers,
734	      runs: records.allRuns,
735	      bridgeError: error,
736	    });
737	    if (!isTransientSupervisorError(error)) {
738	      frontendErrors.push(buildAppError(error, {
739	        source: "Agent runtime",
740	        action: "Stream live agent state",
741	      }));
742	    }
743	  }
744	
745	  return buildEventPayload(records, agentsData, frontendErrors, options, workerEntrySeqs);
746	}

760	function parseLastEventId(raw: string | null | undefined): number | string | null {
761	  if (!raw) {
762	    return null;
763	  }
764	  const trimmed = raw.trim();
765	  if (!trimmed) {
766	    return null;
767	  }
768	  if (parseEventStreamId(trimmed)) {
769	    return trimmed;
770	  }
771	  if (/^\d+$/.test(trimmed)) {
772	    const parsed = Number(trimmed);
773	    return Number.isSafeInteger(parsed) ? parsed : null;
774	  }
775	  return null;
776	}

778	export const handleEventsRequest: OmniHttpHandler = async (request, context) => {
779	  const url = new URL(request.url);
780	  const isSnapshot = url.searchParams.get("snapshot") === "1";
781	  const persistedOnly = url.searchParams.get("persisted") === "1";
782	  const probe = isSnapshot
783	    ? startSlowProbe(`GET /api/events?snapshot=1${persistedOnly ? "&persisted=1" : ""}${url.searchParams.get("runId") ? `&runId=${url.searchParams.get("runId")}` : ""}`)
784	    : null;
785	  const ticketAuth = isSnapshot
786	    ? null
787	    : await redeemStreamTicketRequest(request, "/api/events");
788	  if (ticketAuth?.response) {
789	    probe?.end();
790	    return ticketAuth.response;
791	  }
792	  const auth = ticketAuth
793	    ? { session: null, response: null }
794	    : await requireApiSession(request, {
795	      source: "Events",
796	      action: "Stream live updates",
797	    });
798	  probe?.mark("auth");
799	  if (auth.response) {
800	    probe?.end();
801	    return auth.response;
802	  }
803	
804	  const eventPayloadOptions = {
805	    selectedRunId: url.searchParams.get("runId"),
806	  } satisfies EventPayloadOptions;
807	
808	  if (isSnapshot) {
809	    const payload = persistedOnly
810	      // `persisted=1` is the canonical verification surface used after
811	      // lifecycle mutations. It must reflect SQLite now, even when a route
812	      // bundle did not share the in-process notification version.
813	      ? await buildPersistedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions, probe ?? undefined)
814	      : await (async () => {
815	        const { ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted } = await import("@/server/supervisor/runtime-watchdog");
816	        await ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted();
817	        probe?.mark("ensureSupervisor");
818	        return buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions, probe ?? undefined);
819	      })();
820	    probe?.mark("payload.total");
821	    const requestedChecksum = url.searchParams.get("checksum")?.trim() || "";
822	
823	    // Anchor the snapshot to the current cursor so a subsequent SSE
824	    // connection can pass `Last-Event-ID: <lastEventId>` (or
825	    // `?lastEventId=`) and receive only events newer than this body.
826	    // Exposed as a response header to avoid changing the JSON shape
827	    // that the UI consumes.
828	    const response = Response.json(
829	      requestedChecksum && requestedChecksum === payload.snapshotChecksum
830	        ? {
831	          notModified: true,
832	          snapshotChecksum: payload.snapshotChecksum,
833	          workerEntrySeqs: payload.workerEntrySeqs,
834	        }
835	        : payload,
836	    );
837	    response.headers.set("x-omni-last-event-id", getEventStreamCursor());
838	    if (payload.snapshotChecksum) {
839	      response.headers.set("x-omni-snapshot-checksum", payload.snapshotChecksum);
840	    }
841	    probe?.end();
842	    return response;
843	  }
844	
845	  const { ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted } = await import("@/server/supervisor/runtime-watchdog");
846	  await ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted();
847	
848	  const lastEventIdHeader = request.headers.get("last-event-id");
849	  const resumeFromHeader = parseLastEventId(lastEventIdHeader);
850	  const hasCursorQuery = url.searchParams.has("cursor");
851	  const resumeFromCursorQuery = parseLastEventId(url.searchParams.get("cursor"));
852	  const resumeFromLegacyQuery = parseLastEventId(url.searchParams.get("lastEventId"));
853	  const resumeFromId = hasCursorQuery
854	    ? resumeFromCursorQuery

856	  const runIdScope = eventPayloadOptions.selectedRunId ?? null;
857	  const authenticatedSessionId = ticketAuth?.session?.id ?? auth.session?.id ?? null;
858	
859	  let streamClosed = false;
860	  let unsubscribeRevocation: (() => void) | null = null;
861	  const stream = createBoundedByteStream({
862	    async start(controller) {
863	      const encoder = new TextEncoder();
864	      let lastUpdatePayload = "";
865	      let lastDeliveredId = resumeFromId ?? getEventCursor();
866	      // Cursor tracking the highest id we've already streamed to this
867	      // client; used to drain only newly-buffered named events on each
868	      // poll iteration without re-emitting events we already replayed.
869	
870	      const writeFrame = (id: string, event: string, serializedData: string) => {
871	        if (!controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(
872	          `id: ${id}\nevent: ${event}\ndata: ${serializedData}\n\n`,
873	        ))) {
874	          streamClosed = true;
875	        }
876	      };
877	      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
878	      const sendEvent = (event: string, data: any, id: string) => {
879	        writeFrame(id, event, JSON.stringify(data));
880	      };

883	          if (

893	              reason: revocation.reason,

900	      }
901	      const drainBufferedEvents = (options: { throughId?: number | null } = {}) => {
902	        const replay = getNamedEventsSince(lastDeliveredId, {
903	          runId: runIdScope,
904	          throughId: options.throughId,
905	        });

907	          const marker = recordSnapshotMarker(
908	            getEventStreamNotificationVersion(),
909	            runIdScope,
910	          );
911	          sendEvent(
912	            "stream.resync_required",
913	            { reason: replay.resyncReason ?? "cursor_evicted" },
914	            marker.streamId,
915	          );

917	          return;

941	        drainBufferedEvents();

978	      let hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = false;

980	      // what the build covered, so a wake carrying only delta-only events is
981	      // recognisable and does not force an immediate rebuild.
982	      let snapshotVersionAtLastBuild = getEventStreamSnapshotVersion();

986	          notificationVersionAtStart = getEventStreamNotificationVersion();
987	          snapshotVersionAtLastBuild = getEventStreamSnapshotVersion();
988	          lastSnapshotBuiltAt = Date.now();
989	          drainBufferedEvents();
990	          const runtimePayloadPromise = buildSharedRuntimeEnrichedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions);
991	          const runtimePayload = hasDeliveredRuntimePayload
992	            ? await runtimePayloadPromise
993	            : await Promise.race([
994	              runtimePayloadPromise,
995	              delay(RUNTIME_AGENT_GRACE_MS).then(() => null),
996	            ]);

1000	            hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = true;
1001	          } else {
1002	            sendUpdateIfChanged(await buildSharedPersistedEventPayload(eventPayloadOptions));
1003	            const enrichedPayload = await runtimePayloadPromise;
1004	            if (!streamClosed) {

1006	              hasDeliveredRuntimePayload = true;
1007	            }
1008	          }
1009	          // Named events emitted during snapshot construction must be
1010	          // flushed before we park; otherwise a worker.* event fired
1011	          // mid-build would wait an entire idle cycle to reach the
1012	          // client.

1018	            runIdScope,
1019	          );

1021	            source: "Events",

1095	      "Connection": "keep-alive",
1096	    },
