2	 * Execution event artifact adapter.
3	 *
4	 * Replaces direct `db.insert(executionEvents).values({...})` writes.
5	 *
6	 * Write flow (artifact-first, then SQLite row):
7	 *   1. Resolve / create the run's `execution_events` artifact stream row.
8	 *   2. Reserve the next seq and append the JSON envelope to the JSONL.
9	 *   3. INSERT the `execution_events` row with `artifact_seq` set,
10	 *      `details=NULL`, `details_hash` and a short `details_preview`.
11	 *   4. Commit the cursor in `artifact_streams`.
12	 *
13	 * If step 2 fails: nothing is written, caller surfaces the error.
14	 * If step 3 fails: the artifact record is orphaned and gets cleaned by
15	 *   the repair scan. We do NOT silently fall back to a legacy write —
16	 *   silent fallbacks make migrations untestable.
17	 *
18	 * Read flow:
19	 *   - Rows with `artifact_seq IS NOT NULL` resolve `details` from the
20	 *     artifact stream on demand (legacy `details` column ignored).
21	 *   - Rows with `artifact_seq IS NULL` keep using the legacy `details`
22	 *     column. This is the only supported fallback path.
23	 */
24	import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
25	import { and, asc, desc, eq, inArray, isNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
26	import { db } from "@/server/db";
27	import { executionEvents } from "@/server/db/schema";
28	import { appendArtifactLine } from "@/server/artifacts/append-only-store";
29	import { emitNamedEvent } from "@/server/events/named-events";
30	import {
31	  buildArtifactPreview,
32	  commitArtifactAppend,
33	  ensureArtifactStreamRow,
34	  hashArtifactPayload,
35	  readArtifactStreamMetadata,
36	  reserveNextArtifactSeq,
37	} from "@/server/artifacts/stream-metadata";
38	import { readAllArtifactEntries } from "@/server/artifacts/append-only-store";
39	import type { ArtifactRecordEnvelope } from "@/server/artifacts/stream-types";
40	
41	export interface RecordExecutionEventInput {
42	  runId: string;
43	  workerId?: string | null;
44	  planItemId?: string | null;
45	  eventType: string;
46	  /**
47	   * Domain-specific payload. Stored as the artifact record's `payload`
48	   * and (truncated) in `details_preview` for hot snapshots.
49	   *
50	   * Pre-existing call sites passed a serialized JSON string as
51	   * `details`. The adapter accepts either: a string is wrapped as
52	   * `{ legacy: string }` so canonical hashing/preview still works.
53	   */
54	  details?: unknown;
55	  /** Optional explicit id (otherwise generated). */
56	  id?: string;
57	  /** Optional createdAt override (otherwise now). */
58	  createdAt?: Date;
59	}
60	
61	export interface ExecutionEventRecord {
62	  id: string;
63	  runId: string;
64	  workerId: string | null;
65	  planItemId: string | null;
66	  eventType: string;
67	  details: string | null;
68	  detailsHash: string | null;
69	  detailsPreview: string | null;
70	  artifactSeq: number | null;
71	  createdAt: Date;
72	}
73	
74	function normalizePayload(input: unknown): unknown {
75	  if (input === undefined) return null;
76	  if (typeof input === "string") {
77	    // Try to parse a JSON string back into structured form so
78	    // downstream hashing/preview is stable across writers.
79	    try {
80	      return JSON.parse(input);
81	    } catch {
82	      return input;
83	    }
84	  }
85	  return input;
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * Write an execution event. Returns the persisted record id and seq.
90	 */
91	export async function recordExecutionEvent(input: RecordExecutionEventInput): Promise<{ id: string; artifactSeq: number }> {
92	  const id = input.id ?? randomUUID();
93	  const createdAt = input.createdAt ?? new Date();
94	  const payload = normalizePayload(input.details);
95	  const detailsHash = payload === null ? null : hashArtifactPayload(payload);
96	  const detailsPreview = payload === null ? null : buildArtifactPreview(payload);
97	
98	  const { location } = await ensureArtifactStreamRow({
99	    runId: input.runId,
100	    kind: "execution_events",
101	    ownerId: null,
102	  });
103	  const seq = await reserveNextArtifactSeq({
104	    runId: input.runId,
105	    kind: "execution_events",
106	    ownerId: null,
107	  });
108	
109	  const envelope: ArtifactRecordEnvelope = {
110	    id,
111	    seq,
112	    runId: input.runId,
113	    kind: "execution_events",
114	    createdAt: createdAt.toISOString(),
115	    payload,
116	  };
117	  try {
118	    await appendArtifactLine(location, JSON.stringify(envelope));
119	  } catch (error) {
120	    emitNamedEvent({
121	      kind: "artifact.append_failed",
122	      runId: input.runId,
123	      streamKind: "execution_events",
124	      ownerId: null,
125	      seq,
126	      reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
127	    });
128	    throw error;
129	  }
130	
131	  // Dual-write `details` for the migration window: artifact stream is
132	  // the new source of truth (artifact_seq + the JSONL payload) but the
133	  // legacy `details` column stays populated so any reader that hasn't
134	  // moved to the adapter yet still gets full bodies. Once every reader
135	  // is migrated, switch this back to `details: null` and the artifact
136	  // becomes the only durable copy.
137	  await db.insert(executionEvents).values({
138	    id,
139	    runId: input.runId,
140	    workerId: input.workerId ?? null,
141	    planItemId: input.planItemId ?? null,
142	    eventType: input.eventType,
143	    details: payload === null ? null : typeof payload === "string" ? payload : JSON.stringify(payload),
144	    artifactSeq: seq,
145	    detailsHash,
146	    detailsPreview,
147	    createdAt,
148	  });
149	
150	  await commitArtifactAppend({
151	    streamId: { runId: input.runId, kind: "execution_events", ownerId: null },
152	    seq,
153	    recordId: id,
154	  });
155	  return { id, artifactSeq: seq };
156	}
157	
158	// --- Read paths ----------------------------------------------------
159	
160	interface ExecutionEventRow {
161	  id: string;
162	  runId: string;
163	  workerId: string | null;
164	  planItemId: string | null;
165	  eventType: string;
166	  details: string | null;
167	  detailsHash: string | null;
168	  detailsPreview: string | null;
169	  artifactSeq: number | null;
170	  createdAt: Date;
171	}
172	
173	/**
174	 * Hot-path snapshot list: returns up to `limit` most-recent events for
175	 * a run, with the SHORT preview only (no artifact body read). Use this
176	 * for diagnostics or list views that don't need full bodies.
177	 */
178	export async function listExecutionEventSummariesForSnapshot(
179	  runId: string,
180	  limit: number,
181	): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
182	  return db
183	    .select()
184	    .from(executionEvents)
185	    .where(eq(executionEvents.runId, runId))
186	    .orderBy(desc(executionEvents.createdAt), desc(executionEvents.id))
187	    .limit(limit);
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * Selected-run snapshot read used by `/api/events?snapshot=1`. Returns
192	 * up to `limit` most-recent events with full `details` hydrated from
193	 * the artifact stream. One forward stream read per snapshot — the
194	 * `readEntriesByKey`-style cache in the bytes layer keeps repeat polls
195	 * cheap when the file hasn't moved.
196	 */
197	export async function listExecutionEventsForSnapshot(
198	  runId: string,
199	  limit: number,
200	): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
201	  const rows = await db
202	    .select()
203	    .from(executionEvents)
204	    .where(eq(executionEvents.runId, runId))
205	    .orderBy(desc(executionEvents.createdAt), desc(executionEvents.id))
206	    .limit(limit);
207	  return hydrateExecutionEventDetails(rows);
208	}
209	
210	/**
211	 * Full-body read: returns all events for a run with `details` resolved
212	 * (artifact payload re-serialized as a JSON string for callers that
213	 * still expect the column shape). Used by readers that need the
214	 * complete history (CLI runner, etc.).
215	 */
216	export async function listExecutionEventsForRun(runId: string): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
217	  const rows = await db
218	    .select()
219	    .from(executionEvents)
220	    .where(eq(executionEvents.runId, runId))
221	    .orderBy(asc(executionEvents.createdAt), asc(executionEvents.id));
222	  return hydrateExecutionEventDetails(rows);
223	}
224	
225	/**
226	 * Backward-compatible reader that returns events filtered by worker.
227	 * Used by handoff/request and similar surfaces.
228	 */
229	export async function listExecutionEventsForWorker(
230	  workerId: string,
231	  limit?: number,
232	): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
233	  const query = db
234	    .select()
235	    .from(executionEvents)
236	    .where(eq(executionEvents.workerId, workerId))
237	    .orderBy(desc(executionEvents.createdAt), desc(executionEvents.id));
238	  const rows = limit ? await query.limit(limit) : await query;
239	  return hydrateExecutionEventDetails(rows);
240	}
241	
242	async function hydrateExecutionEventDetails(rows: ExecutionEventRow[]): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
243	  if (rows.length === 0) return rows;
244	
245	  // Group rows that need artifact hydration by runId so we read each
246	  // stream at most once.
247	  const needsHydration: Map<string, ExecutionEventRow[]> = new Map();
248	  for (const row of rows) {
249	    if (row.artifactSeq != null && row.details === null) {
250	      const bucket = needsHydration.get(row.runId) ?? [];
251	      bucket.push(row);
252	      needsHydration.set(row.runId, bucket);
253	    }
254	  }
255	  if (needsHydration.size === 0) return rows;
256	
257	  const detailsById = new Map<string, string>();
258	  for (const [runId, bucket] of needsHydration) {
259	    const meta = await readArtifactStreamMetadata({
260	      runId,
261	      kind: "execution_events",
262	      ownerId: null,
263	    });
264	    if (!meta) {
265	      // No artifact stream yet — these rows must be backfill-pending.
266	      // Leave details null; callers can render from preview/hash.
267	      continue;
268	    }
269	    const { resolveArtifactStreamLocation } = await import("@/server/artifacts/append-only-store");
270	    const location = await resolveArtifactStreamLocation(
271	      {
272	        runId,
273	        kind: "execution_events",
274	        ownerId: null,
275	        projectPath: meta.projectPath,
276	      },
277	      "read",
278	    );
279	    const envelopes = await readAllArtifactEntries<ArtifactRecordEnvelope>(location);
280	    const byId = new Map(envelopes.map((env) => [env.id, env] as const));
281	    for (const row of bucket) {
282	      const env = byId.get(row.id);
283	      if (env) {
284	        detailsById.set(row.id, typeof env.payload === "string" ? env.payload : JSON.stringify(env.payload));
285	      } else {
286	        // Row has artifactSeq + nulled legacy `details`, but the
287	        // envelope wasn't found in the stream — surface so an operator
288	        // can run the repair script.
289	        emitNamedEvent({
290	          kind: "artifact.payload_missing",
291	          runId,
292	          streamKind: "execution_events",
293	          ownerId: null,
294	          seq: row.artifactSeq,
295	          recordId: row.id,
296	        });
297	      }
298	    }
299	  }
300	  return rows.map((row) => (
301	    detailsById.has(row.id)
302	      ? { ...row, details: detailsById.get(row.id) ?? null }
303	      : row
304	  ));
305	}
306	
307	/**
308	 * Delete every execution event row for a run. The associated artifact
309	 * stream files are cleaned by the shared artifact cleanup helper, not
310	 * here, so this is symmetric with the existing SQL-only delete path.
311	 */
312	export async function deleteExecutionEventsForRun(runId: string): Promise<void> {
313	  await db.delete(executionEvents).where(eq(executionEvents.runId, runId));
314	}
315	
316	export async function deleteExecutionEventsForPlanItem(planItemId: string): Promise<void> {
317	  await db.delete(executionEvents).where(eq(executionEvents.planItemId, planItemId));
318	}
319	
320	/**
321	 * Lookup support: load events by id (used by repair tooling and tests).
322	 */
323	export async function findExecutionEventsByIds(ids: string[]): Promise<ExecutionEventRow[]> {
324	  if (ids.length === 0) return [];
325	  return db.select().from(executionEvents).where(inArray(executionEvents.id, ids));
326	}
327	
328	/**
329	 * Count of rows still on the legacy `details` column (no artifact_seq).
330	 * Used by backfill verification.
331	 */
332	export async function countLegacyExecutionEvents(): Promise<number> {
333	  const result = await db
334	    .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)` })
335	    .from(executionEvents)
336	    .where(isNull(executionEvents.artifactSeq));
337	  return Number(result[0]?.count ?? 0);
338	}

444	                                </span>
445	                              ) : null}
446	                              {showCompletedAttentionIndicator && statusIndicatorLabel && !showAwaitingUserIndicator ? (
447	                                <span
448	                                  className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-sky-300"
449	                                  aria-label={statusIndicatorLabel}
450	                                  role="img"
451	                                  title={statusIndicatorLabel}
452	                                />
453	                              ) : null}
454	                            </span>
455	                            <span
456	                              className={cn("inline-flex h-5 w-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md border", visualConfig.className)}
457	                              title={t("conversation.sidebar.conversationVisual", { kind: visualConfig.label })}
458	                              aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.conversationVisual", { kind: visualConfig.label })}
459	                            >
460	                              {visualKind === "direct" ? (
461	                                <CliBrandIcon workerType={run.preferredWorkerType ?? null} className={run.preferredWorkerType === "opencode" ? "h-3 w-3" : "h-3.5 w-3.5"} />
462	                              ) : (
463	                                <ConversationIcon className="h-3.5 w-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />
464	                              )}
465	                            </span>
466	                            {renamingRunId === run.id && renameSource !== "topbar" ? (
467	                              <Input
468	                                value={renameValue}
469	                                onChange={(event) => setRenameValue(event.target.value)}
470	                                onClick={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}
471	                                onKeyDown={(event) => {
472	                                  event.stopPropagation();
473	                                  if (event.key === "Enter") {
474	                                    event.preventDefault();
475	                                    commitRenamingRun(run.id);
476	                                  } else if (event.key === "Escape") {
477	                                    event.preventDefault();
478	                                    cancelRenamingRun();
479	                                  }
480	                                }}
481	                                onBlur={() => commitRenamingRun(run.id)}
482	                                autoFocus
483	                                className="h-7 min-w-0 text-[13px]"
484	                              />
485	                            ) : (
486	                              <span className="truncate text-[13px]">{run.title}</span>
487	                            )}
488	                          </div>
489	                          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-1">
490	                            {run.status === "running" ? (
491	                              <LoaderCircle className="h-3.5 w-3.5 animate-spin text-muted-foreground motion-reduce:animate-none" />
492	                            ) : null}
493	                            {runIsUnread && !showCompletedAttentionIndicator ? (
494	                              <div className="h-2 w-2 shrink-0 rounded-full bg-blue-500" />
495	                            ) : null}
496	                            {canArchiveConversation && isCommitConversation ? (
497	                              <Button
498	                                variant="ghost"
499	                                size="icon"
500	                                className="h-6 w-6 shrink-0 text-muted-foreground opacity-100 hover:text-foreground lg:opacity-0 lg:group-hover:opacity-100"
501	                                aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.archiveConversation", { title: run.title })}
502	                                title={t("conversation.sidebar.archiveConversation", { title: run.title })}
503	                                onClick={(event) => {
504	                                  event.stopPropagation();
505	                                  archiveRun(run);
506	                                }}
507	                              >
508	                                <Archive className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
509	                              </Button>
510	                            ) : null}
511	                            <DropdownMenu>
512	                              <DropdownMenuTrigger
513	                                onClick={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}
514	                                className="inline-flex h-6 w-6 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground opacity-100 transition-colors ring-offset-background hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 lg:opacity-0 lg:group-hover:opacity-100"
515	                                aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.conversationActions", { title: run.title })}
516	                              >
517	                                <MoreHorizontal className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />
518	                              </DropdownMenuTrigger>
519	                              <DropdownMenuContent align="end" className="min-w-28">
520	                                <DropdownMenuItem
521	                                  className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
522	                                  onClick={(event) => {
523	                                    event.stopPropagation();
524	                                    startRenamingRun(run);
525	                                  }}
526	                                >
527	                                  <Pencil className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.rename")}
528	                                </DropdownMenuItem>
529	                                {canMoveConversation ? (
530	                                  <DropdownMenuItem
531	                                    className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
532	                                    onClick={(event) => {
533	                                      event.stopPropagation();
534	                                      startMovingRun(run);
535	                                    }}
536	                                  >
537	                                    <FolderInput className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.moveToProject")}
538	                                  </DropdownMenuItem>
539	                                ) : null}
540	                                {canArchiveConversation ? (
541	                                  <DropdownMenuItem
542	                                    className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
543	                                    onClick={(event) => {
544	                                      event.stopPropagation();
545	                                      archiveRun(run);
546	                                    }}
547	                                  >
548	                                    <Archive className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.archive")}
549	                                  </DropdownMenuItem>
550	                                ) : null}
551	                                <DropdownMenuItem
552	                                  variant="destructive"
553	                                  className="cursor-pointer whitespace-nowrap"
554	                                  onClick={(event) => {
555	                                    event.stopPropagation();
556	                                    deleteRun(run);
557	                                  }}
558	                                >
559	                                  <Trash2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.delete")}
560	                                </DropdownMenuItem>
561	                              </DropdownMenuContent>
562	                            </DropdownMenu>
563	                          </div>
564	                        </div>
565	                      </div>
566	                    </div>
567	                  );
568	                })}
569	                {hiddenSessionCount > 0 ? (
570	                  <button
571	                    type="button"
572	                    className="ml-7 mt-1 inline-flex h-7 items-center rounded-md px-2 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:bg-muted/60 hover:text-foreground focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
573	                    aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.showMoreSessions", {
574	                      count: nextSessionBatchCount,
575	                      project: group.name,
576	                    })}
577	                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.showMoreSessions", {
578	                      count: nextSessionBatchCount,
579	                      project: group.name,
580	                    })}
581	                    onClick={() => onShowMoreProjectSessions(group.path)}
582	                  >
583	                    {t("conversation.sidebar.moreSessions")}
584	                  </button>
585	                ) : null}
586	              </div>
587	            </div>
588	          </Collapsible>
589	        );
590	      })}
591	    </>
592	  );
593	}

595	interface MoveRunToProjectDialogProps {
596	  open: boolean;
597	  moveRunProjectPath: string;
598	  moveRunToProjectOptions: string[];
599	  isMoveRunToProjectPending: boolean;
600	  setMoveRunProjectPath: (value: string) => void;
601	  confirmMoveRunToProject: () => void;
602	  cancelMovingRun: () => void;
603	}
604	
605	function MoveRunToProjectDialog({
606	  open,
607	  moveRunProjectPath,
608	  moveRunToProjectOptions,
609	  isMoveRunToProjectPending,
610	  setMoveRunProjectPath,
611	  confirmMoveRunToProject,
612	  cancelMovingRun,
613	}: MoveRunToProjectDialogProps) {
614	  return (
615	    <Dialog
616	      open={open}
617	      onOpenChange={(nextOpen) => {
618	        if (!nextOpen) {
619	          cancelMovingRun();
620	        }
621	      }}
622	    >
623	      <DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>
624	        <DialogHeader>
625	          <DialogTitle>{t("conversation.moveProject.title")}</DialogTitle>
626	          <DialogDescription>
627	            {moveRunToProjectOptions.length > 0
628	              ? t("conversation.moveProject.description")
629	              : t("conversation.moveProject.empty")}
630	          </DialogDescription>
631	        </DialogHeader>
632	        <div className="grid gap-2">
633	          <label className="text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground" htmlFor="move-run-project-select">
634	            {t("conversation.moveProject.projectLabel")}
635	          </label>
636	          <select
637	            id="move-run-project-select"
638	            className="h-9 w-full rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm text-foreground shadow-xs outline-none transition-colors focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60"
639	            value={moveRunProjectPath}
640	            onChange={(event) => setMoveRunProjectPath(event.target.value)}
641	            disabled={isMoveRunToProjectPending || moveRunToProjectOptions.length === 0}
642	          >
643	            <option value="">{t("conversation.moveProject.placeholder")}</option>
644	            {moveRunToProjectOptions.map((projectPath) => (
645	              <option key={projectPath} value={projectPath}>
646	                {projectPath}
647	              </option>
648	            ))}
649	          </select>
650	        </div>
651	        <DialogFooter>
652	          <Button
653	            type="button"
654	            variant="outline"
655	            onClick={cancelMovingRun}
656	            disabled={isMoveRunToProjectPending}
657	          >
658	            {t("common.cancel")}
659	          </Button>
660	          <Button
661	            type="button"
662	            onClick={confirmMoveRunToProject}
663	            disabled={!moveRunProjectPath || isMoveRunToProjectPending}
664	          >
665	            {t("conversation.moveProject.ok")}
666	          </Button>
667	        </DialogFooter>
668	      </DialogContent>
669	    </Dialog>
670	  );
671	}

726	/**
727	 * Memoized. Every SSE frame gave the shell a new state identity and re-rendered
728	 * this entire subtree, even when nothing it renders had changed. Its props are
729	 * spread from `sharedSidebarProps`, whose callbacks are now stable, so the
730	 * shallow comparison is meaningful.
731	 */
732	const ConversationSidebar = memo(function ConversationSidebar({
733	  filteredProjects,
734	  activeProjects,
735	  conversationSidebarTab,
736	  setConversationSidebarTab,
737	  isHydratingConversations,
738	  searchQuery,
739	  setSearchQuery,
740	  selectedRunId,
741	  messages,
742	  readMarkers,
743	  collapsedProjectPaths,
744	  visibleProjectSessionCounts,
745	  onProjectOpenChange,
746	  onReorderProjects,
747	  onCollapseAllProjects,
748	  onShowMoreProjectSessions,
749	  setShowSettings,
750	  openOnboarding,
751	  openFolderPicker,
752	  startNewPlan,
753	  beginConversationInProject,
754	  autoCommitProject,
755	  isAutoCommitProjectPending,
756	  handleRemoveProject,
757	  selectRun,
758	  renamingRunId,
759	  renameValue,
760	  renameSource,
761	  setRenameValue,
762	  movingRunId,
763	  moveRunProjectPath,
764	  moveRunToProjectOptions,
765	  setMoveRunProjectPath,
766	  startMovingRun,
767	  confirmMoveRunToProject,
768	  cancelMovingRun,
769	  isMoveRunToProjectPending,
770	  startRenamingRun,
771	  commitRenamingRun,
772	  cancelRenamingRun,
773	  archiveRun,
774	  deleteRun,
775	  authEnabled,
776	  openPairDeviceDialog,
777	  logout,
778	  themeMode,
779	  setThemeMode,
780	  onCollapse,
781	  onOpenExternalSessions,
782	  runnerControlsMode = "desktop",
783	}: ConversationSidebarProps) {
784	  useI18nSnapshot();
785	  const themeModeLabel = t(themeMode === "night" ? "theme.mode.switchDay" : "theme.mode.switchNight");
786	  const visibleProjectGroups = conversationSidebarTab === "projects" ? filteredProjects : activeProjects;
787	  const hasExpandedVisibleProjectGroup = visibleProjectGroups.some((group) => !collapsedProjectPaths.has(group.path));
788	  const mounted = useSyncExternalStore(
789	    useCallback((listener) => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.subscribe(listener), []),
790	    useCallback(() => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.getSnapshot(), []),
791	    () => conversationSidebarHydrationManager.getSnapshot(),
792	  );
793	  useEffect(() => {
794	    conversationSidebarHydrationManager.markMounted();
795	  }, []);
796	
797	  if (!mounted) {
798	    // First render (SSR + initial client paint) renders an empty shell so the
799	    // client tree shape matches the server's. Without this, the project/run
800	    // list populates from local state after hydration, shifting Base UI's
801	    // auto-generated IDs and producing a hydration mismatch warning across
802	    // every DropdownMenuTrigger in the sidebar.
803	    return (
804	      <div
805	        className="relative flex h-full min-h-0 w-full flex-col overflow-hidden bg-[#f1f1f0] dark:bg-muted/30"
806	        aria-hidden="true"
807	      />
808	    );
809	  }
810	
811	  return (
812	    <div className="relative flex h-full min-h-0 w-full flex-col overflow-hidden bg-[#f1f1f0] dark:bg-muted/30">
813	      <div className="space-y-1 px-3 pb-3 pt-2 lg:px-3 lg:pb-3 lg:pt-2">
814	        <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
815	          <div className="hidden min-w-0 flex-1 items-center gap-2 lg:flex">
816	            <OmniHarnessMark className="h-8 w-8" />
817	            <span className="min-w-0 truncate text-sm font-semibold text-[#333333] dark:text-zinc-100">
818	              {PRODUCT_NAME}
819	            </span>
820	          </div>
821	          {onCollapse ? (
822	            <Button
823	              variant="ghost"
824	              size="icon"
825	              className="hidden h-9 w-9 text-[#333333]/75 transition-all duration-150 ease-out hover:bg-[#deddda] hover:text-[#1f1f1f] lg:inline-flex dark:text-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-muted/70 dark:hover:text-zinc-100 motion-reduce:transition-none"
826	              aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.collapseAria")}
827	              title={t("conversation.sidebar.collapseAria")}
828	              onClick={onCollapse}
829	            >
830	              <PanelLeftClose className="h-4 w-4 transition-transform duration-150 ease-out group-hover/button:-translate-x-0.5 motion-reduce:transition-none" />
831	            </Button>
832	          ) : null}
833	        </div>
834	        <RunnerControls
835	          placement="sidebar"
836	          controlId={runnerControlsMode === "mobile" ? "runner-switcher-mobile" : "runner-switcher"}
837	          renderDialogs={runnerControlsMode === "desktop"}
838	        />
839	        <div className="flex items-stretch gap-0">
840	          <Button variant="ghost" className="h-9 min-w-0 flex-1 justify-start px-2 text-sm text-[#333333] hover:bg-[#deddda] hover:text-[#1f1f1f] dark:text-zinc-200 dark:hover:bg-muted/70 dark:hover:text-zinc-100" onClick={startNewPlan}>
841	            <Plus className="mr-2 h-4 w-4 shrink-0" /> {t("conversation.sidebar.newSession")}
842	          </Button>
843	          {onOpenExternalSessions && (

846	                className="inline-flex h-9 w-8 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md text-[#333333]/60 transition-colors hover:bg-[#deddda] hover:text-[#1f1f1f] focus-visible:outline-none dark:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-muted/70 dark:hover:text-zinc-100"
847	                aria-label={t("externalSessions.moreOptionsAria")}
848	              >

856	            </DropdownMenu>
857	          )}
858	        </div>

861	          <Input
862	            type="text"
863	            placeholder={t("conversation.sidebar.searchPlaceholder")}
864	            value={searchQuery}
865	            onChange={(e) => setSearchQuery(e.target.value)}
866	            className="h-9 w-full border-transparent bg-[#e4e3e1] pl-8 text-sm text-[#333333] transition-all placeholder:text-[#333333]/75 hover:bg-[#deddda] focus-visible:border-[#c8c7c5] focus-visible:bg-[#e4e3e1] focus-visible:ring-1 dark:bg-white/[0.08] dark:text-zinc-100 dark:placeholder:text-zinc-400 dark:hover:bg-white/[0.095] dark:focus-visible:bg-white/[0.08]"
867	          />
868	        </div>
869	      </div>
870	
871	      <div className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden">
872	        <ScrollArea className="h-full px-3">
873	          <div className="space-y-3 pb-4 pt-0.5">
874	          <div className="ml-2 mr-1 flex items-center justify-between">
875	            <div className="flex items-center gap-1">
876	              <button
877	                type="button"
878	                onClick={() => setConversationSidebarTab("projects")}
879	                className={cn(
880	                  "rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold transition-colors",
881	                  conversationSidebarTab === "projects"
882	                    ? "bg-[#deddda] text-[#1f1f1f] dark:bg-white/[0.12] dark:text-zinc-100"
883	                    : "text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
884	                )}
885	              >
886	                {t("conversation.sidebar.tab.projects")}
887	              </button>
888	              <button
889	                type="button"
890	                onClick={() => setConversationSidebarTab("recent")}
891	                className={cn(
892	                  "rounded px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold transition-colors",
893	                  conversationSidebarTab === "recent"
894	                    ? "bg-[#deddda] text-[#1f1f1f] dark:bg-white/[0.12] dark:text-zinc-100"
895	                    : "text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground",
896	                )}
897	              >
898	                {t("conversation.sidebar.tab.active")}
899	              </button>
900	            </div>
901	            <div className="flex items-center gap-0.5">
902	              <Tooltip>
903	                <TooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex" />}>
904	                  <Button
905	                    variant="ghost"
906	                    size="icon"
907	                    className="h-6 w-6 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"
908	                    disabled={!hasExpandedVisibleProjectGroup}
909	                    aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.collapseAllProjects")}
910	                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.collapseAllProjects")}
911	                    onClick={() => onCollapseAllProjects(visibleProjectGroups.map((group) => group.path))}
912	                  >
913	                    <ListChevronsDownUp className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />

915	                </TooltipTrigger>
916	                <TooltipContent side="bottom" align="end">
917	                  {t("conversation.sidebar.collapseAllProjects")}

919	              </Tooltip>
920	              <Tooltip>
921	                <TooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex" />}>
922	                  <Button
923	                    variant="ghost"
924	                    size="icon"
925	                    className="h-6 w-6 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"
926	                    aria-label={t("conversation.sidebar.addProject")}
927	                    title={t("conversation.sidebar.addProject")}

933	                <TooltipContent side="bottom" align="end">
934	                  {t("conversation.sidebar.addProject")}
935	                </TooltipContent>
936	              </Tooltip>
937	            </div>
938	          </div>
939	
940	          {conversationSidebarTab === "projects" ? (
941	            <ConversationProjectGroupList
942	              groups={filteredProjects}
943	              isHydratingConversations={isHydratingConversations}
944	              selectedRunId={selectedRunId}
945	              messages={messages}
946	              readMarkers={readMarkers}
947	              collapsedProjectPaths={collapsedProjectPaths}
948	              visibleProjectSessionCounts={visibleProjectSessionCounts}
949	              canReorderProjects={conversationSidebarTab === "projects"}
950	              onProjectOpenChange={onProjectOpenChange}
951	              onReorderProjects={onReorderProjects}
952	              onShowMoreProjectSessions={onShowMoreProjectSessions}
953	              beginConversationInProject={beginConversationInProject}
954	              autoCommitProject={autoCommitProject}
955	              isAutoCommitProjectPending={isAutoCommitProjectPending}
956	              handleRemoveProject={handleRemoveProject}
957	              selectRun={selectRun}
958	              renamingRunId={renamingRunId}
959	              renameValue={renameValue}
960	              renameSource={renameSource}
961	              setRenameValue={setRenameValue}
962	              startMovingRun={startMovingRun}
963	              startRenamingRun={startRenamingRun}
964	              commitRenamingRun={commitRenamingRun}
965	              cancelRenamingRun={cancelRenamingRun}
966	              archiveRun={archiveRun}
967	              deleteRun={deleteRun}
968	              emptyState={<p className="pl-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">{t("conversation.sidebar.empty.projects")}</p>}

40	function timestampMs(value: string | null | undefined) {

46	function hasSuccessfulRecoveryAfterFailure(run: RunRecord, events: ExecutionEventRecord[]) {
47	  if (run.status !== "failed") {
48	    return false;
49	  }
50	
51	  const failureTime = timestampMs(run.failedAt ?? run.updatedAt ?? run.createdAt);
52	  if (failureTime === null) {

55	
56	  return events.some((event) => {
57	    if (!RECOVERY_SUCCESS_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.eventType)) {
58	      return false;
59	    }
60	    const eventTime = timestampMs(event.createdAt);
61	    return eventTime !== null && eventTime >= failureTime;
62	  });

22	/**
23	 * True when a rebuilt state carries nothing the current one does not already
24	 * have, so the incoming copy can be dropped and the existing object identity
25	 * kept.
26	 *
27	 * The server stamps every snapshot with `snapshotChecksum` over the whole
28	 * payload (`server/events/payload-checksum.ts`), so an equal checksum means an
29	 * identical server-side view. Comparing the merged arrays by identity would be
30	 * useless here — a re-delivered payload is a fresh `JSON.parse`, so every array
31	 * is a new object even when byte-identical. The checksum is the only cheap
32	 * signal that actually distinguishes "same data" from "new data".

34	 * Scope-defining fields are still compared, because a frame that only switches
35	 * `snapshotRunId` must not be swallowed just because the catalog hashed the

39	 * mutation, `snapshotChecksum` still reflects the last *server* view, so a poll
40	 * that re-delivers that same view would otherwise revert the optimistic change
41	 * and flicker until the server caught up.

43	function isNoOpSnapshotUpdate(current: EventStreamState, next: EventStreamState) {
44	  const checksum = next.snapshotChecksum;
45	  if (!checksum || checksum !== current.snapshotChecksum) {
46	    return false;
47	  }
48	
49	  return next.snapshotRunId === current.snapshotRunId
50	    && next.snapshotSource === current.snapshotSource
51	    && next.messageScope?.complete === current.messageScope?.complete;

102	/**
103	 * Which surface owns a message once its send settles.
104	 *
105	 * The server can answer with both a delivered message row and the queue row it
106	 * was released from. The transcript renders the message row and the drawer
107	 * renders the queue row, so leaving both in place shows the user their message
108	 * twice with nothing to reconcile them — the two lists dedup independently.
109	 *
110	 * This used to be keyed on `busyAction === "steer"`, which only covered a
111	 * client that had correctly predicted a busy conversation. A stale idle
112	 * prediction sends no `busyAction` at all, and that path kept both rows. The
113	 * presence of a delivered message row is the fact that actually decides it.
114	 */
115	export function resolveQueuedMessageRowAfterSend(result: {
116	  message?: { id: string } | null;
117	  queuedMessage?: { id: string } | null;
118	}): "hide" | "upsert" | "none" {
119	  if (!result.queuedMessage) {
120	    return "none";
121	  }
122	  return result.message ? "hide" : "upsert";
123	}

145	function mergeOutputEntries(
146	  current: AgentSnapshot["outputEntries"],
147	  loaded: AgentSnapshot["outputEntries"],
148	) {
149	  const byId = new Map<string, NonNullable<AgentSnapshot["outputEntries"]>[number]>();
150	  for (const entry of loaded ?? []) {
151	    byId.set(entry.id, entry);
152	  }
153	  for (const entry of current ?? []) {
154	    byId.set(entry.id, entry);
155	  }
156	  return Array.from(byId.values()).sort((first, second) => {
157	    const timeDelta = timestampMs(first.timestamp) - timestampMs(second.timestamp);
158	    return timeDelta !== 0 ? timeDelta : first.id.localeCompare(second.id);
159	  });
160	}

169

200	export function applyStopWorkerOptimisticUpdate(
201	  current: EventStreamState,

204	) {
205	  const now = new Date().toISOString();
206	  const run = current.runs.find((candidate) => candidate.id === runId) ?? null;

210	  const workers = (current.workers || []).map((worker) => {
211	    if (worker.runId !== runId) {
212	      return worker;
213	    }
214	    if (
215	      worker.id === workerId
216	      || (isImplementationRun && isOptimisticallyStoppableWorkerStatus(worker.status))
217	    ) {
218	      stoppedWorkerIds.add(worker.id);
219	      return { ...worker, status: "cancelled", updatedAt: now };
220	    }
221	    return worker;
222	  });
223	
224	  const hasActiveWorker = workers.some((worker) =>
225	    worker.runId === runId && isOptimisticallyStoppableWorkerStatus(worker.status));
226	  const nextRunStatus = isImplementationRun
227	    ? "awaiting_user"
228	    : hasActiveWorker
229	      ? run?.status
230	      : "cancelled";

232	  return {
233	    ...current,

242	        : agent),
243	    executionEvents: [

248	        details: {

11	function parseTimestampMs(value: string | null | undefined): number {
12	  if (!value) return 0;
13	  const t = new Date(value).getTime();
14	  return Number.isFinite(t) ? t : 0;

17	function laterOf(a: string | null | undefined, b: string | null | undefined): string | null {
18	  const aMs = parseTimestampMs(a);

20	  if (!a && !b) return null;
21	  return aMs >= bMs ? (a ?? null) : (b ?? null);

25	  return values.reduce<string | null>((acc, v) => laterOf(acc, v), null);

72	/**
73	 * Per-run rollups computed in ONE pass over each global collection.
74	 *
75	 * Without this, classifying N runs cost N full scans of every message, queued
76	 * message, worker and agent in the app — and the sidebar did that three times
77	 * over on every SSE frame, allocating two `Date` objects per message compared.
78	 * With ~40 runs and a few thousand accumulated messages that is hundreds of
79	 * thousands of iterations per frame, which is what made the sidebar the single
80	 * most expensive thing on the client's main thread while sessions streamed.
81	 *
82	 * Build once with `buildSidebarActivityIndex`, reuse for every run.
83	 */
84	export interface SidebarActivityIndex {
85	  latestMessageAtByRunId: Map<string, string>;
86	  latestUserInputAtByRunId: Map<string, string>;
87	  workersByRunId: Map<string, WorkerInput[]>;
88	  agentsByWorkerId: Map<string, AgentInput>;

91	export function buildSidebarActivityIndex(args: {
92	  messages: MessageInput[];
93	  queuedMessages: QueuedMessageInput[];
94	  workers: WorkerInput[];
95	  agents: AgentInput[];
96	}): SidebarActivityIndex {
97	  const latestMessageAtByRunId = new Map<string, string>();
98	  const latestUserInputAtByRunId = new Map<string, string>();
99	  const workersByRunId = new Map<string, WorkerInput[]>();
100	  const agentsByWorkerId = new Map<string, AgentInput>();
101	
102	  const keepLater = (map: Map<string, string>, runId: string, value: string | null | undefined) => {
103	    if (!value) return;
104	    const existing = map.get(runId);
105	    if (!existing || parseTimestampMs(value) > parseTimestampMs(existing)) {
106	      map.set(runId, value);
107	    }
108	  };
109	
110	  for (const message of args.messages) {
111	    keepLater(latestMessageAtByRunId, message.runId, message.createdAt);
112	    if (isUserInputMessage(message)) {
113	      keepLater(latestUserInputAtByRunId, message.runId, message.createdAt);
114	    }
115	  }
116	
117	  for (const queued of args.queuedMessages) {
118	    keepLater(
119	      latestUserInputAtByRunId,
120	      queued.runId,
121	      queued.deliveredAt ?? queued.updatedAt ?? queued.createdAt,
122	    );
123	  }
124	
125	  for (const worker of args.workers) {
126	    const bucket = workersByRunId.get(worker.runId);
127	    if (bucket) {
128	      bucket.push(worker);
129	    } else {
130	      workersByRunId.set(worker.runId, [worker]);
131	    }
132	  }
133	
134	  for (const agent of args.agents) {
135	    agentsByWorkerId.set(agent.name, agent);
136	  }
137	
138	  return { latestMessageAtByRunId, latestUserInputAtByRunId, workersByRunId, agentsByWorkerId };
139	}

178	function getIndexedSidebarRunLastActivityAt(
179	  args: Pick<SidebarRunActivityArgs, "run" | "workerOutputObservedAtByRunId">,
180	  index: SidebarActivityIndex,
181	): string | null {
182	  const userInputAt = index.latestUserInputAtByRunId.get(args.run.id) ?? null;

187	function getIndexedWorkingActivityAt(run: RunInput, index: SidebarActivityIndex): string | null {
188	  const runWorkers = index.workersByRunId.get(run.id) ?? [];
189	  const timestamps: (string | null | undefined)[] = [run.updatedAt];
190	
191	  for (const worker of runWorkers) {
192	    if (isWorkerActiveStatus(worker.status)) {
193	      timestamps.push(worker.updatedAt);
194	    }
195	    const agent = index.agentsByWorkerId.get(worker.id);
196	    if (agent && isWorkerActiveStatus(agent.state)) {
197	      timestamps.push(agent.updatedAt);
198	    }
199	  }
200	
201	  timestamps.push(run.createdAt);
202	  return maxTimestamp(...timestamps);
203	}

216	function isIndexedSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking(run: RunInput, index: SidebarActivityIndex): boolean {
217	  // Terminal runs are never "working" — stale worker metadata loses.
218	  if (isTerminalRunStatus(run.status)) return false;
219	
220	  const normalizedStatus = normalizeRunStatus(run.status);
221	  if (normalizedStatus === "needs_recovery") return false;
222	
223	  if (normalizedStatus !== "running" && normalizedStatus !== "awaiting_user") return false;
224	
225	  const runWorkers = index.workersByRunId.get(run.id) ?? [];
226	
227	  for (const worker of runWorkers) {
228	    if (isWorkerActiveStatus(worker.status)) return true;
229	    const agent = index.agentsByWorkerId.get(worker.id);
230	    if (agent && isWorkerActiveStatus(agent.state)) return true;
231	  }
232	
233	  // Run is "running" with no active workers/agents yet — still counts.
234	  return normalizedStatus === "running";
235	}

255	export function classifyIndexedSidebarRun(
256	  args: Pick<SidebarRunActivityArgs, "run" | "readMarkers" | "workerOutputObservedAtByRunId" | "nowMs" | "selectedRunId">,
257	  index: SidebarActivityIndex,
258	): RunActiveClassification {
259	  const { run, readMarkers, nowMs } = args;
260	  const lastReadAt = readMarkers[run.id] ?? null;
261	  const normalizedStatus = normalizeRunStatus(run.status);
262	
263	  const latestUnreadAt = getIndexedRunLatestUnreadTimestamp(run, index);
264	  const isUnread = isRunUnread({ latestMessageAt: latestUnreadAt, lastReadAt });
265	
266	  const isWorking = isIndexedSidebarRunCurrentlyWorking(run, index);
267	
268	  const recentActivityAt = getIndexedSidebarRunLastActivityAt(args, index);
269	  const allowsRecentActivity = normalizedStatus !== "cancelled" && normalizedStatus !== "canceled";
270	  const isRecent =
271	    allowsRecentActivity &&
272	    recentActivityAt !== null &&
273	    nowMs - parseTimestampMs(recentActivityAt) <= ACTIVE_SESSION_ACTIVITY_WINDOW_MS;
274	
275	  const isSelected = args.selectedRunId != null && args.run.id === args.selectedRunId;
276	  const isActive = isUnread || isWorking || isRecent || isSelected;
277	
278	  let activeSortAt: string | null = recentActivityAt;
279	  if (isUnread && latestUnreadAt) {
280	    activeSortAt = maxTimestamp(activeSortAt, latestUnreadAt);
281	  }
282	  if (isWorking) {
283	    activeSortAt = maxTimestamp(activeSortAt, getIndexedWorkingActivityAt(run, index));
284	  }
285	  if (!activeSortAt) activeSortAt = run.createdAt;
286	
287	  return { isActive, isUnread, isWorking, isRecent, recentActivityAt, activeSortAt };
288	}

290	export function compareActiveSidebarRunsDesc(
291	  a: { activeSortAt: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
292	  b: { activeSortAt: string | null; createdAt: string; id: string },
293	): number {
294	  const diff = parseTimestampMs(b.activeSortAt) - parseTimestampMs(a.activeSortAt);
295	  if (diff !== 0) return diff;
296	  const createdDiff = parseTimestampMs(b.createdAt) - parseTimestampMs(a.createdAt);
297	  if (createdDiff !== 0) return createdDiff;
298	  return a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0;
299	}

301	export interface BuildActiveGroupsArgs {
302	  groups: SidebarGroup[];
303	  messages: MessageInput[];
304	  readMarkers: Record<string, string>;
305	  workers: WorkerInput[];
306	  agents: AgentInput[];

311	}
312	
313	export function buildActiveConversationGroups(args: BuildActiveGroupsArgs): SidebarGroup[] {
314	  const { groups, messages, readMarkers, workers, agents, queuedMessages, workerOutputObservedAtByRunId, nowMs, selectedRunId } = args;
315	
316	  const activeGroups: Array<{ group: SidebarGroup; latestActivityMs: number }> = [];
317	
318	  // One pass over the global collections, reused for every run below. This
319	  // replaces N full scans of messages/queued/workers/agents per frame.
320	  const index = buildSidebarActivityIndex({ messages, queuedMessages, workers, agents });
321	
322	  for (const group of groups) {
323	    const activeRuns: Array<SidebarRun & { activeSortAt: string | null }> = [];
324	    let groupLatestMs = 0;
325	
326	    for (const run of group.runs) {
327	      const result = classifyIndexedSidebarRun({
328	        run: {
329	          id: run.id,
330	          status: run.status,
331	          createdAt: run.createdAt,
332	          updatedAt: (run as SidebarRun & { updatedAt?: string | null }).updatedAt ?? null,
333	        },
334	        readMarkers,
335	        workerOutputObservedAtByRunId,
336	        nowMs,
337	        selectedRunId,
338	      }, index);
339	
340	      if (!result.isActive) continue;
341	
342	      activeRuns.push({ ...run, activeSortAt: result.activeSortAt });
343	      const ms = parseTimestampMs(result.activeSortAt);
344	      if (ms > groupLatestMs) groupLatestMs = ms;
345	    }
346	
347	    if (activeRuns.length === 0) continue;
348	
349	    activeRuns.sort(compareActiveSidebarRunsDesc);
350	
351	    activeGroups.push({
352	      group: { path: group.path, name: group.name, runs: activeRuns },
353	      latestActivityMs: groupLatestMs,
354	    });
355	  }
356	
357	  activeGroups.sort((a, b) => {
358	    const diff = b.latestActivityMs - a.latestActivityMs;
359	    if (diff !== 0) return diff;
360	    if (a.group.name < b.group.name) return -1;
361	    if (a.group.name > b.group.name) return 1;
362	    if (a.group.path < b.group.path) return -1;
363	    if (a.group.path > b.group.path) return 1;
364	    return 0;
365	  });
366	
367	  return activeGroups.map((entry) => entry.group);

370	// Apply search to the active groups.
371	// If the query matches the project name, all active sessions in that project remain visible.
372	// Otherwise filter active sessions whose title or path matches the query.
373	export function filterActiveConversationGroups(
374	  activeGroups: SidebarGroup[],
375	  searchQuery: string,
376	): SidebarGroup[] {
377	  if (!searchQuery) return activeGroups;
378	  const q = searchQuery.toLowerCase();
379	
380	  return activeGroups
381	    .map((group) => {
382	      if (group.name.toLowerCase().includes(q)) {
383	        // Project name matches — show all active sessions in this project.
384	        return group;
385	      }
386	      // Otherwise filter sessions by title or path.
387	      const runs = group.runs.filter(
388	        (run) => run.title.toLowerCase().includes(q) || run.path.toLowerCase().includes(q),
389	      );
390	      return { ...group, runs };
391	    })
392	    .filter((group) => group.runs.length > 0);
393	}

## Summary: Cheaply Queryable Per-Run "Last Agent Turn Finished" Signals

| Signal Source | Table | Key Columns | Indexed? | Scoped to Run? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Last execution event** | `executionEvents` | `run_id, created_at, eventType` | Yes | Yes (scoped in snapshot) | Use `eventType` to filter for "turn_finished" events |
| **Worker idle transition** | `workers` | `run_id, status, updatedAt` | Yes (via `run_id`) | Yes | Query `WHERE run_id = ? AND status = 'idle'` → `MAX(updatedAt)` |
| **Worker entry stream** | `artifact_streams` | `run_id, kind='worker_entries', updatedAt` | Yes (via composite index) | Yes | Last per-stream append tracked via `artifact_streams.updatedAt` |
| **Run general activity** | `runs` | `updatedAt` | Yes (via `created_at` indexes) | N/A | Coarse-grained; bumped on any run mutation |

**Recommended approach:** Query the intersection of:
1. `workers WHERE run_id = ? AND status = 'idle'` (ordered by `updatedAt DESC LIMIT 1`)
2. Most recent `executionEvents WHERE run_id = ? AND eventType LIKE '%complete%'` (if you need confirmation event)
3. Check `artifact_streams WHERE run_id = ? AND kind = 'worker_entries' AND ownerId = ?` for `updatedAt` per worker

All three paths are efficiently indexed and scoped to the selected run.

AND status = 'idle'` (ordered by `updatedAt DESC LIMIT 1`)\n2. Most recent `executionEvents WHERE run_id = ? AND eventType LIKE '%complete%'` (if you need confirmation event)\n3. Check `artifact_streams WHERE run_id = ? AND kind = 'worker_entries' AND ownerId = ?` for `updatedAt` per worker\n\nAll three paths are efficiently indexed and scoped to the selected run."
  }

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-07T11:45:30.926Z

The solution needs to live server-side with a persisted `lastActivityAt` field on the runs table that gets updated when user messages are inserted or when an agent turn completes. The key is identifying the turn boundary—where the worker transitions from active to idle in sync.ts, which aligns with the `worker_turn_completed` execution event.

For sorting, I should handle this client-side in buildConversationGroups rather than in the database queries, since that's where optimistic merges happen and it'll keep the ordering deterministic. The backfill strategy is to set `lastActivityAt` to the maximum of the run's creation time and the latest message timestamp, with a SQL migration that captures this across messages and artifact streams.

Writing SQL migration... The performance concern with rebuilding snapshots on every SSE frame makes the derived approach risky. A hybrid solution makes more sense: use a persisted column updated through a single helper function called at key chokepoints like message inserts and worker status transitions, with lazy backfill as a safety net. This keeps writes centralized and error-prone, avoiding the cost of recomputing aggregates on hot paths.

The real question is whether to persist the column or compute it at query time—that's a genuine fork that changes the implementation scope. I should present the analysis and recommendation, then ask the user which approach they prefer since it affects the schema and work involved.

## Claude · 2026-08-07T11:45:56.242Z

## What's actually happening

Two separate code paths, and only one of them is broken the way you describe:

- **Recent/Active tab** already sorts by activity (`compareActiveSidebarRunsDesc`, `src/interface/home/sidebar-activity.ts:290`) using a composite `activeSortAt`.
- **Projects tab** has **no sort at all** client-side. `buildConversationGroups` (`src/lib/conversations.ts:41`) preserves whatever order the server sent, and the server sends `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` — `src/runtime/http/routes/events.ts:97` and the duplicate at `src/server/events/persisted-snapshot.ts:238`. So yes: creation date.

Side effect worth knowing: because there's no client sort, `EventStreamStateManager`'s merge appends unseen runs to the *end* of the array, so an optimistically-created run can land at the bottom of its project until the next full snapshot.

## The blocker

The signal you want isn't available where the sort happens.

1. **Messages are scoped to the selected run only.** `selectedMessageRunIds` (`events.ts:293`) returns just the selected run (+ its parent for implementation mode); with nothing selected the query returns `[]` (`events.ts:127`). So the client literally has no message timestamps for the other 99% of sessions in the sidebar.
2. **Finalized agent turns aren't in `messages` at all.** Worker response text moved out of the DB into the per-worker JSONL stream — see the comment at `send-message.ts:1102` ("the legacy role:'worker' messages row is gone"). Execution events, including `worker_turn_completed`, are likewise fetched only for the selected run (`events.ts:170`).
3. **`runs.updatedAt` is not a usable proxy.** ~70 write sites bump it, including memory consolidation, runtime watchdog health checks, git auto-commit, quota recovery, project-path canonicalization and agent-generated title updates. Sorting on it would shuffle idle sessions to the top for pure bookkeeping.

So this can't be fixed by adding a `.sort()` in `conversations.ts`. It needs a per-run activity timestamp that exists server-side for *every* run.

## Two ways to get one

**A. Persisted `runs.lastActivityAt` column** (my recommendation). Add the column via the existing ad-hoc migration pattern (`src/server/db/index.ts` — `tableColumns()` check + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`, bump `DB_SCHEMA_VERSION`), write it from a single `touchRunActivity(runId, at)` helper called at exactly two chokepoints:
- user message insert — the ~18 `db.insert(messages)` sites filtered to real user input (excluding `internal`/`intervention`, matching the existing `isUserInputMessage` rule at `sidebar-activity.ts:29`), plus queued-message delivery;
- agent turn finalization — the worker `working → idle` transition in `src/server/conversations/sync.ts:688`, which is the one path all session types go through (the `worker_turn_completed` execution event only fires for supervised runs).

Then `ORDER BY last_activity_at DESC` in both snapshot queries **and** an explicit sort in `buildConversationGroups`, so optimistic merges can't scramble it. One-time backfill: `MAX(created_at, max(messages.created_at), max(artifact_streams.updated_at WHERE kind='worker_entries'))`.

Cost: two files to migrate, and a risk of missing a write site later.

**B. Derive at snapshot time** — LEFT JOIN two aggregates (`MAX(messages.created_at)` and `MAX(artifact_streams.updated_at)` for `kind='worker_entries'`) onto the runs query. No schema change, no backfill, can't drift out of sync. Cost: a `GROUP BY` over the whole messages table on every snapshot build, and snapshots get rebuilt on SSE frames — that's the exact hot path the perf comment at `sidebar-activity.ts:72-82` was written about.

I lean A: correctness under load matters more here, and the two chokepoints are narrow enough to be maintainable.

Two things I'd keep unchanged unless you say otherwise: the Recent tab's existing `activeSortAt` logic, and the ordering of the project groups themselves (currently your explicit-projects order).

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-07T13:44:03.989Z

Instead of modifying all the message insert sites, I could use a SQLite trigger on the messages table that automatically updates `runs.last_activity_at` when a user message is inserted, filtering out internal message kinds. This approach is more robust since it can't be missed by future code changes, and the codebase already uses triggers for similar patterns like the worker timers.

For agent turn finalization, I'd add another trigger that fires when a worker's status transitions out of the working state, updating the run's last activity timestamp. But I need to be careful here — a worker leaving the working state doesn't always mean the turn is finalized; it could transition to stuck or cred-exhausted states. I should restrict the trigger to only fire when the status becomes idle, and I'll need to check the status vocabulary and the worker status utilities to make sure I'm using the right condition.

There's also the question of write amplification since sync.ts updates workers frequently, though the trigger would only fire on actual status transitions out of working, which is bounded. And I should verify that sync.ts actually does write a working→idle transition at the end of a turn before committing to this approach.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-07T13:44:44.303Z

I'm going with a triggers approach to handle both signals. I'll set up a trigger that fires when a user message is inserted—specifically when the role is 'user' and the kind isn't marked as 'internal' or 'intervention'—to update the runs table accordingly.

Now I'm realizing there's a nuance with the 'checkpoint' kind. The sidebar activity excludes it, but that's because it's looking at a different signal (queuedMessages deliveredAt). For detecting actual user input to the database, checkpoint is the kind used when messages are sent to workers, so I need to include it rather than exclude it. The exclusions should be just 'internal' and 'intervention'. There's also a consideration that when messages are copied during fork or promotion operations, they'll carry the original created_at timestamp, which is harmless since it represents a real user message anyway.

Actually, there's a timing issue here. When a run is forked, the copied messages have old timestamps, so the new run's last_activity_at could end up earlier than its own creation time. The cleaner approach is to initialize last_activity_at to the run's created_at when the run is created, then let the trigger only move it forward. That way a forked run starts at its own creation time and older copied messages can't drag the activity timestamp backward. I can either use a trigger on run insertion to set it, or make the column nullable and use COALESCE in the sort, but the guard logic needs to compare against the run's created_at rather than NULL to avoid old messages setting it too early.

Setting up a database trigger... Finishing the trigger condition...

I'm deciding whether to restrict the final status to just 'idle' or allow any exit from 'working' — including 'stuck', 'error', or 'cancelled'. Since a finalized turn is still activity worth tracking regardless of how it ended, I'll keep it broad to match the existing work-timer semantics. Now I need to verify the execution order: the trigger block runs after the column addition, so the `last_activity_at` column will already exist when these triggers are created.

For fresh databases, I'll add the column directly in the initial `CREATE TABLE` statement at line 36, and for existing databases, I'll use an `ALTER TABLE`. After that, I'm backfilling existing rows by computing the maximum timestamp across created_at, the latest user message, artifact stream updates, and worker updates. I'll include both the worker_entries stream and user messages for the most faithful representation of agent activity, keeping created_at as the baseline. Since artifact_streams might not exist on older databases, I need to verify it's handled in the initial schema setup. Now I'm checking how Drizzle stores timestamps — whether it's using seconds or milliseconds for the unix epoch in libsql/sqlite. Adding the database index and coalesce logic for safety, then I need to find where runs get serialized in those files and update the type definitions across home-types, conversations, and the client-side sorting logic.

  "new_string": "if (!messageColumnNames.has(\"attachments_json\")) {\n  await client.execute(\"ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN attachments_json text;\");\n}\n\n// ── runs.last_activity_at ──────────────────────────────────────────\n// Sidebar ordering needs \"when did this conversation last do something a human\n// would recognise\" — the last user message, or the last agent turn that\n// finished. `runs.updated_at` cannot answer that: ~70 call sites bump it,\n// including memory consolidation, the runtime watchdog, git auto-commit, quota\n// recovery and agent-generated titles, all of which would float dormant\n// sessions to the top.\n//\n// Maintained by triggers rather than by a `touchRunActivity()` helper on purpose:\n// user rows enter `messages` from 18 different call sites and turn ends come out\n// of the worker sync loop, so a TS helper is one forgotten call away from\n// silently wrong ordering. Both triggers only ever move the timestamp forward.\n// Must run after the `messages.kind` migration above — the triggers read it.\nawait client.executeMultiple(`\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS runs_activity_seed\nAFTER INSERT ON runs\nWHEN NEW.last_activity_at IS NULL\nBEGIN\n  UPDATE runs SET last_activity_at = NEW.created_at WHERE id = NEW.id;\nEND;\n\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS runs_activity_on_user_message\nAFTER INSERT ON messages\nWHEN lower(NEW.role) = 'user'\n  AND lower(COALESCE(NEW.kind, '')) NOT IN ('internal', 'intervention')\nBEGIN\n  UPDATE runs\n  SET last_activity_at = NEW.created_at\n  WHERE id = NEW.run_id\n    AND COALESCE(last_activity_at, 0) < NEW.created_at;\nEND;\n\nCREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS runs_activity_on_worker_turn_end\nAFTER UPDATE OF status ON workers\nWHEN lower(substr(OLD.status, 1, instr(OLD.status || ':', ':') - 1)) = 'working'\n  AND lower(substr(NEW.status, 1, instr(NEW.status || ':', ':') - 1)) != 'working'\nBEGIN\n  UPDATE runs\n  SET last_activity_at = NEW.updated_at\n  WHERE id = NEW.run_id\n    AND COALESCE(last_activity_at, 0) < NEW.updated_at;\nEND;\n`);\n\n// Backfill rows that predate the triggers. `created_at` is the floor so a forked\n// run — whose copied messages carry the *original* timestamps — can never sort\n// behind its own creation. Historical agent turns aren't in `messages` (worker\n// output lives in the artifact stream), so the stream's `updated_at` stands in.\nawait client.execute(`\n  UPDATE runs\n  SET last_activity_at = MAX(\n    created_at,\n    COALESCE((\n      SELECT MAX(m.created_at) FROM messages m\n      WHERE m.run_id = runs.id\n        AND lower(m.role) = 'user'\n        AND lower(COALESCE(m.kind, '')) NOT IN ('internal', 'intervention')\n    ), 0),\n    COALESCE((\n      SELECT MAX(a.updated_at) FROM artifact_streams a\n      WHERE a.run_id = runs.id AND a.kind = 'worker_entries'\n    ), 0)\n  )\n  WHERE last_activity_at IS NULL;\n`);\n"
}

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-07T13:47:43.219Z

For the Recent/Active tab, I'm weighing whether to pass `lastActivityAt` into `classifyIndexedSidebarRun` to improve sorting consistency with the Projects tab. Using it as a sort fallback would help, but feeding it directly would also change which sessions qualify as "recent/active" within that 20-minute window—shifting tab membership in ways the user didn't request. The safer approach is to use `lastActivityAt` only as a secondary sort criterion rather than altering the tab's membership logic.

## Claude thinking · 2026-08-07T13:47:49.224Z

I'm seeing how the optimistic update logic handles timestamps — when a local change is newer, it spreads the current run over the incoming one, but this overwrites `lastActivityAt` with the optimistic value even though optimistic updates only set `updatedAt` and not `lastActivityAt`. This means `lastActivityAt` could be stale compared to the incoming data, creating a one-frame inconsistency that the client sort resolves by taking the max of `lastActivityAt` and `createdAt`.

## Claude · 2026-08-07T13:54:30.046Z

Done. 2571 passing; the 2 failures are pre-existing and belong to other uncommitted work in this tree (`sync.ts` / `worker-resume.ts` and their tests — files I never touched). I verified the `conversations-sync` one fails identically with my changes stashed away, and `worker-resume` passes in isolation (order-dependent).

## What changed

**The core problem:** the Projects tab had *no sort at all* — it rendered whatever order the server sent, which was `ORDER BY created_at`. And the timestamp you asked for didn't exist anywhere queryable: messages are only loaded for the selected run, agent turn output isn't in the `messages` table at all (it lives in per-worker JSONL artifact streams), and `runs.updatedAt` is bumped by ~70 call sites including memory consolidation, watchdog health checks and auto-commit.

So I added a real activity stamp.

**`runs.last_activity_at`** (`src/server/db/schema.ts`, migration in `src/server/db/index.ts`, schema version 5→6), maintained by three SQL triggers rather than a TS helper — user rows enter `messages` from 18 call sites and turn ends come out of the worker sync loop, so a helper would be one forgotten call away from silently wrong ordering:

- `runs_activity_seed` — new runs start at their creation time.
- `runs_activity_on_user_message` — advances on user rows, skipping `internal`/`intervention`.
- `runs_activity_on_worker_turn_end` — advances when a worker leaves `working`, reusing the status-parsing idiom from the existing work-timer triggers.

Both advancing triggers only ever move the stamp *forward*, so a fork copying older messages in can't drag a run backwards. Existing rows are backfilled from user messages and worker-entry stream timestamps, floored at `created_at`.

**Sorting** now happens in both snapshot queries (`events.ts:97`, `persisted-snapshot.ts:238`) *and* client-side in `buildConversationGroups`. The client sort isn't redundant: `EventStreamStateManager` merges runs by id and appends unseen ones to the end, so an optimistically-created run previously sank to the bottom of its project until the next full snapshot.

**One judgement call worth flagging:** a turn that ends in `stuck` or `error` counts as activity, not just a clean `idle`. That matches the existing work-timer semantics and keeps a session that just failed visible at the top — say the word if you'd rather only clean completions count.

I also made the Recent tab's sort fall back to the persisted stamp instead of creation date. Its worker-output signal is only observed live, so a run whose last turn finished before page load had nothing to sort on. I deliberately did *not* feed the stamp into the 20-minute `isRecent` window — that would change which sessions appear in that tab, which you didn't ask for.

Tests: 7 new trigger/migration tests against a real SQLite file (including the backfill path and the fork-can't-go-backwards case), plus 2 ordering tests for the client sort. I updated one assertion in `events-route.test.ts` that pinned the exact `orderBy` source text — its intent, a stable `id` tie-breaker, still holds.
